In German, there is a special word that resonates with a global community. That word is "Bürgerbewegung" and it translates to “a citizen's movement”. For Enpal, this means a people's movement to take charge of a greener energy supply. Enpal focuses on making a literal change in the world, a portmanteau of “energy” and “pal”. Enpal is not just another solar company: It offers the first integrated solution for the green smart home, including photovoltaic panels, batteries, charging stations for e-vehicles, green electricity tariff, and energy management software. The best part of their business model is that customers rent the energy system in a subscription-style model,  saving the high up-front costs. A recent poll shows that 9 out of 10 Germans favor solar rooftop installations. Enpal works with
qualified
specialist companies and craft businesses
to make that a reality in the best and easiest way possible.
Visit our website
here

cards.quote: Fighting the climate crisis is the greatest challenge of our generation. The Enpal team wants to enable every homeowner to join the fight and become energy-independent by giving them the opportunity to produce green energy without any up-front costs.

content.text: Before they became the first institutional investor during Enpal's Series B funding, HV Capital had developed a relationship with CEO and founder Mario Kohle for over a decade. The first interaction was during Mario's university days when he worked on a website portal for students. Not long after, Mario started Kauferportal, a platform that connects homeowners with home-related products and services, and successfully sold the company to General Atlantic. HV recognised early that Mario was a serial entrepreneur and wouldn't stay idle for long. Mario's next project was much bigger than himself and HV. He founded Enpal with the singular mission of decarbonising Europe, one solar-powered home at a time. HV loves this type of mission-driven founder, as they often possess the grit and determination needed to see a project to completion and beyond. Since then, HV and Mario have been fully unified in the mission to make Europe and the world green and energy-independent.

cards.list_description: Enpal is on a mission to become the energy supplier for the 21 century and has already become Germany's largest photovoltaic systems installers. Vis-a-vis its customers, Enpal offers its "zero-down" PV rental solution with customers paying a monthly rate that includes cost of installations, operations and maintenance. This simplicity turns PV rental into the no-brainer that it should be, paving the way for large-scale decarbonization of electryicity grids.

content.text: For Enpal, the future is bright and sunny. In times of soaring energy prices and a threatening climate crisis, more and more people want to take their energy into their own hands and join the movement to protect the planet for our children. Enpal's business model of no upfront costs and low fixed-lease payments is therefore proving popular. Enpal's invention could be scaled globally and expand into other sectors like e-mobility and community-based energy distribution, connecting humankind into a renewable community.

cards.about: Delivery Hero has been continuously transforming the way people order food online. Instead of ordering by phone or at the door of the restaurant orders and payments can be conveniently placed online. Restaurants are peer-reviewed, making it easier to choose a good restaurant every time. With just a few clicks, delicious food is on the way.
cards.quote:
BACK YOUR WINNING TEAMS FOR THEIR LONG TERM VISION. LEAVE YOUR OWN TACTICS BEHIND.

STAY A BELIEVER BY CONVICTION. STAY A BELIEVER IN SUPERIOR FOUNDERS.

content.text: In 2009 Markus Fuhrman showed up at the HV office in Munich interested in a career in Venture Capital. He had an entrepreneurial background with Mjam, a food delivery service in AT. HV recommended he gained more experience as a business builder and connected him to Team Europe and Lukasz. Markus and Lukasz met and decided to start Lieferheld, the German operation with Fabian Siegel as co-founder in 2010. Sometime later Delivery Hero and Lieferheld merged. An international star was born. Nobody had any clue what Niklas, the founder of Delivery Hero and his AAA-team would build.

HV’s story with Delivery Hero begins with Markus Fuhrman. On recommendation from HV, Markus started to look for experiences as a business builder. This led him to starting Lieferheld, which merged with Delivery Hero.

Delivery Hero is one of the biggest contradictions of HV. They were somehow an enabler of the start of Lieferheld. For fund reasons HV were not able to invest in Delivery Hero as the international partner. Instead, Delivery Hero took the opportunity of an early exit, scared to stay long term for fund reasons. Delivery Hero is now a global masterpiece of a buy and build strategy. When successfully executed, their model can enable young digital companies a fast track to global leadership.

cards.list_description:
Delivery Hero is holding company of several internet platforms where customers can order food (e.g. Pizza, Pasta, Asian Food etc.) quickly and securely and at no extra cost. Choice, convenience, reliability, and quality are the key benefits for the customers. Delivery Hero provides a purely success-related lead generation platform for delivery services. 

Delivery Hero and Lieferheld were merged in February 2012. Lieferheld was founded in September 2010 and is located in Berlin.

content.text: Delivery Hero has created the largest global food network (outside of China) with 500,000+ restaurants on its platform. The company holds a strong position in 36 out of the 42 countries it operates in across Europe, Latin America, Asia-Pacific, the Middle East and North Africa. This relates to terms of restaurants, active users, orders, online and mobile platforms.
Delivery Hero also operates its own delivery service primarily in over 530 cities around the globe. Headquartered in Berlin, Germany, the company has over 22,000 employees.

cards.about: Founded in Berlin in 2011, HelloFresh is the leading global provider of fresh food at home. With their meal kit delivery platform they serve more than four million customers in 14 markets across Europe, the US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand.
cards.quote:
WE ARE EXTREMELY HAPPY AND PROUD TO HAVE HAD SUCH A STRONG PARTNER AT OUR SIDE RIGHT FROM THE BEGINNING. WE IMMEDIATELY KNEW THAT HV WERE THE RIGHT COMPANY TO TEAM UP WITH.

THEY UNDERSTOOD AND BELIEVED IN OUR VISION FROM DAY ONE. SINCE THEN, WE’VE COME A LONG WAY TOGETHER.
cards.founders_names:
Dominik Richter
Thomas Griesel
Jessica Nilsson
cards.how_it_started:
When HV Capital first met the founding team at HelloFresh, people were either looking for recipes in books or online. They would shop for ingredients at grocery stores, or order delivery/take-out from restaurants. HelloFresh brought them something completely new that combined all these elements. It was the team’s original vision to reduce waste and bring fresh products to customers – all of which is fulfilled by the company today.
When HV Capital met the founding team at HelloFresh they were trying to find a sweet spot for consumers between recipe books, fresh ingredients and delivery. In combination with their desire to offer customers something completely new, they also wanted to reduce waste across the board.

HelloFresh started in Germany, and quickly tested in European markets before taking the big step to launch in the US amidst heavy competition. The company eventually became the market leader in all its operating markets. Six years after HV’s initial seed investment, the company went public in 2017 and is now valued at more than €8bn in market capitalization. In Q1 of 2020 HelloFresh delivered more than 100 million meals to its customers around the world.

“At HelloFresh we want to change the way people eat forever. By radically transforming the food supply chain we are offering our customers a better, easier and more sustainable way to shop for groceries. At the same time, we give them access to wholesome, tasty meals with a great value for money. HelloFresh is now a little over eight years old. In this time, we have become one of the planet’s leading providers of fresh food at home and we won’t stop here. We are very excited for everything that is yet to come!” – HelloFresh Founders
cards.list_description:
HelloFresh is a food subscription service with weekly delivery of its boxes to end consumers. It provides its customers with all ingredients and recipes needed to prepare meals at home. With focus on premium quality and ecological foods, an expert team develops exclusive recipes that are easy to cook. HelloFresh operates its market leading service in various European countries and the US.

Prior to Rocket Internet’s successful IPO, HV contributed its stakes in HelloFresh and 6 other companies in exchange for a 2.5% stake in Rocket Internet.
cards.future_perspectives:
HelloFresh aims to provide households with wholesome, home-made, hassle-free meals. Without shopping, customers receive fresh ingredients directly sourced from local producers. HelloFresh contributes significantly to reducing food waste across the entire supply chain by cutting out unnecessary middlemen and providing customers with pre-portioned ingredients.

Behind the scenes is a huge data-driven technology platform, putting them in prime position to leverage subscriber touch points. HelloFresh operates a subscription business model with high flexibility around delivery. This approach can fundamentally change the way consumers shop for, and consume food. Transforming the traditional food supply chain, HelloFresh is at the forefront of disrupting a multi trillion dollar industry that’s at the start of a huge online transition.

cards.about: Zalando SE is Europe's leading online platform for fashion and lifestyle that connects customers, brands and partners in 17 European countries. What started in 2008 as a Berlin-based online shop for shoes became a tech-enabled fashion ecosystem. By merging strong expertise in the fields of fashion, technology and convenience, Zalando aims to become the Starting Point for Fashion – the one destination customers gravitate to when they think about fashion.
cards.quote:
AT A TIME WHEN MANY PEOPLE TOLD US THAT OUR PLANS TO SELL SHOES ONLINE WERE NOTHING BUT CRAZY, HV BELIEVED IN US.

WE ARE STILL GRATEFUL FOR THEIR TRUST AND SUPPORT IN ZALANDO’S EARLY DAYS, BECAUSE WITHOUT BOTH, ZALANDO WOULDN’T BE WHERE WE ARE TODAY.
cards.how_it_started:
In October 2008, David and Robert came back from South America with their first entrepreneurial experiences and great ambitions. From an apartment on Berlin’s Torstrasse (that is still used by the company today), they started Zalando.

When HV Capital first met Zalando, buying sneakers online was anything but easy. Online penetration in the fashion industry was low, and it could take up to several weeks to get a pair of sneakers delivered. People outside of cities had to travel miles to stay up to date with the latest fashion trends, always bound to the limited offers of local retailers. Today they can have them delivered straight to their door at any time, thanks to Zalando.
cards.list_description:
Zalando is the leading European online shoe and fashion e-commerce player. With its special focus on high customer satisfaction, comprehensive service and short delivery times, Zalando offers a wide spectrum of shoes, clothing and accessories for men, women and children. It is market leader in most of the 14 countries it currently operates in.

In October 2014, Zalando successfully IPOed in Frankfurt in one of the largest European internet IPOs ever.
cards.future_perspectives:
Today, a world without Zalando is difficult to imagine. Since 2008, the company has grown from an e-commerce store for shoes to a platform for fashion and lifestyle with almost 14,000 employees. They aim to be the Starting Point for Fashion, and a sustainable platform with a net-positive impact for people and the planet. David and Robert are still members of the Zalando management board – together with Rubin, who joined slightly later – actively managing day to day operations. They have also become active angel investors, contributing to the emergence of several other new companies in Europe.

As an online platform for fashion and lifestyle, Zalando brings together around 32 million active customers in Europe, more than 2,500 brands and many other partners. They are aware that this gives them a unique opportunity to help shape the fashion industry for the better, and Zalando is committed to this goal.

cards.about: Designer. Preloved. Vintage. Streetwear. Sneakers. Whatever your style. Find it on Depop. Depop is the fashion marketplace app where the next generation comes to discover and buy unique items.
cards.quote: DEPOP WANTS TO BREAK THE CURRENT FASHION SYSTEM BY BRINGING IT TO A PLACE WHERE THERE IS A MORE RESPONSIBLE CONSUMPTION. AND WE DO THIS BY WORKING WITH UNIQUE AND INSPIRING CREATIVES WHO CARE ABOUT PRODUCTS WHICH CAN LAST FOREVER.
cards.slogan: One of the world's largest fashion communities.
cards.how_it_started: In 2012 Lars’ friend Roberto invited him to a place close to Venice where Italian companies were being incubated. Depop was called Garage back in the days and the founder Simon Beckermann was sitting in a small black cube trying to revolutionize the way people shop fashion items. After many discussions about the changing fashion landscape and its consumer behavior (and some proper Italian food) they decided to work together.
cards.list_description: Depop is the mobile marketplace for anyone to buy and sell almost anything straight from their mobile. If you can photograph it, you can sell it. Users follow their favourite individuals, shops and brands to discover what they buy, sell and like, or open their own little mobile shop with the touch of a button.
cards.future_perspectives: Depop today is one of the world`s largest fashion communities around the globe, with more than 15 million users in 147 countries listing more than 100.000 items a day and growing. Depop is about to become the global conduit of connection, not only in m-commerce, but culture, design, and creative communities around the world. With a global community buying, selling and connecting to make fashion more inclusive, diverse and less wasteful. This is what transforming fashion looks like. “Lars’ experience and his straightforward thinking that focuses on areas of improvement are an extremely helpful ingredient for the success of Depop. We spent a lot of time together, especially during the early years when Depop was still vulnerable…I know that I can fully trust and rely on Lars and his partners who have supported and invested into Depop across all financing rounds in the past eight years, thus becoming Depop`s largest shareholder.” – Simon Beckerman, Depop Founder

content.text: FlixMobility is a global mobility provider, offering new alternatives for convenient, affordable and environmentally-friendly travel via the FlixBus, FlixTrain, FlixCar and FlixBus Charter brands. Thanks to a unique business model and innovative technology, FlixMobility quickly established as Europe's largest long-distance travel network.

cards.quote:
HV CAPITAL HAS ALWAYS BEEN A PERFECT SPARRING PARTNER ACROSS A VARIETY OF TOPICS AND WE HAVE A VERY TRUSTFUL RELATIONSHIP.

TOGETHER WITH HV CAPITAL WE WILL ACCELERATE OUR GROWTH TO OFFER SMART AND SUSTAINABLE TRAVEL OPTIONS TO EVEN MORE PEOPLE ACROSS THE WORLD
cards.founders_names:
Jochen Engers
André Schwämmlein
Daniel Krauss
Torben Greve
Panya Putsathit

content.text: When HV Capital first met the founders of FlixBus, long-distance bus transportation between major cities did not really exist yet. In 2009 the three FlixBus founders André, Daniel and Jochen learned that the German long-distance travel sector was going to be liberalized and saw a unique chance to build up a completely new mobility service with the once-in-a-lifetime situation of the deregulation of the German market. They had little in common with the bus industry, apart from organizing bus trips to Austrian ski resorts during their student days and using the public city buses. Nevertheless, all founders were very interested in the industry and in creating a completely new means of transport. Since 2013 FlixMobility is changing the way people travel throughout Europe and the US. Based on a proprietary technology platform, a strong focus on customer experience and brand as well as the partnering with traditional transportation partners, Flix combines strengths from two worlds to form one customer-oriented service offering. In 2018 FlixMobility launched the first green long-distance FlixTrains as well as pilot projects for all-electric buses in France. FlixMobility launched FlixBus USA to bring this new travel alternative to the United States later in the same year. Today, FlixMobility is offering mobility services in 35 countries for millions of customers.

cards.list_description: FlixBus is a long-distance bus operator based in Munich and Berlin. Since its official start in April 2012, FlixBus has become a major player in the European long-distance bus market. Together with a strong partner network of medium-sized bus operators, the company offers an extensive route network throughout Germany and neighbouring countries, and a unique offer in terms of quality, comfort, sales and service.

content.text: The vision of FlixMobility is to offer smart and green mobility for everyone to experience the world. To provide services for comfortable and convenient travelling to all passengers FlixMobility is constantly improving its services and investing into technology and innovation.

Flank is an AI automation platform for expert teams. With Flank, expert teams —such as legal, privacy, compliance, info-sec, and finance—can train and deploy specialized AI Agents that offer 24/7 support to commercial teams.

cards.quote:
GOING INTO THIS AS FIRST-TIME FOUNDERS, WE COULDN’T HAVE ASKED FOR A BETTER PARTNER. HV HAS BEEN INCREDIBLY SUPPORTIVE – CHALLENGING US TO BE BETTER WHILE WATCHING OUT FOR OUR WELL-BEING.

ABOVE ALL, HV HAS CONTINUED TO BELIEVE IN AND CHAMPION OUR VISION.
cards.slogan: Your expert team's first AI colleague
cards.founders_names:
Lilian Breidenbach
Charlotte Kufus
Jacob Jones

content.text: Flank met HV in spring 2018 at a 15-minute Q&A organized by TU University. Back then, Flank was called Legal OS and its team of four (pre-product) spearheading a bold vision of making legal knowledge more accessible. Keeping a close eye on their progress, HV was impressed and invested a year later.
Flank has since developed a category-leading solution with strong product-market fit attracting customers such as TravelPerk, DeepL, Mural, DocPlanner, and others.

cards.list_description: Flank is an AI automation platform for expert teams. With Flank, expert teams —such as legal, privacy, compliance, info-sec, and finance—can train and deploy specialized AI Agents that offer 24/7 support to commercial teams.

content.text: Every year, billions are spent on process optimization, employee training, and the latest efficiency software. However, the primary source of operational drag is often overlooked: waiting for expert support. Friction increases as the company grows. Flank’s mission is to eliminate this friction by removing the bottlenecks altogether and enabling commercial teams to make decisions (and close deals!) faster. This is achieved by empowering the business with expertise on-demand via Flank agents - a major step towards
an organization without bottlenecks

cards.about: ottonova is pioneering the private health insurance industry in Germany, aiming to reinvent the way customers interact with their insurance provider. They offer digital, user-friendly services, with a wide range of health insurance products. Over the last three years ottonova have launched award-winning products and grown their audience to more than 5,000 customers.
cards.quote: HV WAS ALWAYS A VERY ACTIVE INVESTOR WITH A KEEN INTEREST IN THE BUSINESS. LEVERAGING THEIR EXPERIENCE AND NETWORK HELPED US IN ALL ASPECTS.
cards.founders_names:
Dr. Roman Rittweger
Sebastian Scheerer
Frank Birzle
cards.how_it_started: HV’s relationship with ottonova founder Roman Rittweger goes back a long way. Initially launched to pioneer telemedicine in Germany, the company has now transformed into a leading health insurance platform. Despite being met initially with conservative and cautious market reactions they have developed a new experience of digital health services since launching in 2015.
cards.list_description: It is ottonova’s mission to shape healthcare provision in a new, simple and transparent way. ottonova wants to be your partner concerning all healthcare-related issues. Personal, direct and innovative.
cards.future_perspectives: ottonova aims to lead digital-only health insurance in Germany and Europe, disrupting a stagnant market with a strong emphasis on service. With one integrated platform they deliver simple, transparent insurance and health products to private and business clients. For customers ottonova is a pocket doctor, using the digital world to help them to live their healthiest lives.

meta.title: Agreena
meta.description: Agreena unlocks the power of soil carbon removals and natural capital to finance the transition to regenerative agriculture. Working in close collaboration with partner farmers across 16 European markets and growing, AgreenaCarbon is the world’s leading soil carbon platform. Combined with market leading satellite monitoring technologies, Agreena’s solutions can support farmers, companies, and governments on the road to net zero.

content.text: Agreena unlocks the power of soil carbon removals and natural capital to finance the transition to regenerative agriculture. Working closely with partner farmers across 16 European markets and growing, AgreenaCarbon is the world’s leading soil carbon platform. With market-leading satellite monitoring technologies, Agreena’s solutions can support farmers, companies, and governments on the road to net zero.

cards.slogan: Scaling regenerative agriculture through finance and technology.
cards.founders_names:
Simon Haldrup
Julie Koch Fahler
Ida Boesen

content.text: Over the span of two decades, Kinnevik and HV Capital have meticulously crafted a partnership rooted in trust and mutual respect. Their collaborative efforts have been instrumental in the ascendancy of eminent brands including Zalando, Delivery Hero, and Home24. In the nascent stages of their partnership, Climate Tech remained peripheral. However, as the European ecosystem matured, echoing the global shift towards sustainability, Climate Tech transformed into a point of strategic interest.

At HV Capital Alex and Jannis, whose exploided for two years the Climate Tech landscape before discovering Agreena. Hailing from the fertile innovation soil of Copenhagen, Agreena stood at the crossroads of Climate Tech, Fintech, and Agtech, showcasing a multi-faceted approach to environmental solutions. Kinnevik, as one of the early believers in Agreena's vision, laid the foundational trust that would subsequently be built upon. With a rich reservoir of in-house expertise and the catalytic influence of the enduring partnership with Kinnevik, HV Capital emerged not just as investors but as trusted allies to Agreena's founding trio - Julie Koch Fahler, Ida Boesen, and Simon Haldrup.

Leading Agreena's Series B funding round with investors like Giant Ventures, re:Food, Aenu, and Vaeksfonden was more than a financial endeavor for HV Capital; it was a forward leap into a future where technology and climate coalesce into solutions that transcend contemporary boundaries and redefine sustainable innovation.

Agreena stands at the forefront of a global movement, pioneering a carbon farming platform that is not just innovative but transformative, serving farmers worldwide in their transition to regenerative agriculture. In a world where agriculture is a significant contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, Agreena emerges as a beacon of change, illuminating pathways where agriculture transforms from a challenge to a solution.

By bridging Climate Tech with Fintech and Agtech, Agreena catalyzes a global adoption of sustainable practices through its financial reward schemes, offering tangible incentives for ecological farming transitions. Beyond its financial mechanisms, Agreena carries a deeper vision – to sow the seeds for a future where farming nourishes a planet abundant in biodiversity, food safety, sustainability, and health, with technology as the cornerstone of this green revolution.

cards.about: Started in Munich back in 2014, Scalable Capital is Europe’s leading wealth management platform. They offer their robo- advice based approach directly to customers via two models - direct B2C, and B2B2C together with large institutional partners to their respective client base.
cards.quote: ONE OF THE BEST VC’S IN MY VIEW. THEY BEHAVE LIKE ENTREPRENEURS, HAVE THE RARE ABILITY TO KNOW WHAT’S IMPORTANT AND WHAT’S NOT, ARE VERY FAST AND ARE GENUINELY NICE PEOPLE.
cards.founders_names:
Erik Podzuweit
Florian Prucker
Patrick Pöschl
Prof. Dr. Stefan Mittnik
Adam French
cards.how_it_started: When HV Capital first met the founding team of Scalable Capital, people did not have access to smart automated investment platforms. Instead, they would have had to choose a set of ETF to strategically invest their money and rebalance such portfolios all the time. As this is almost impossible for a normal person, the team of Scalable wanted to solve that dilemma with technology. And bring algorithms so far only accessible to large customers of big investment banks to the mass market of end customers. Scalable started in the UK and Germany, became licensed by the financial authorities in both geographies and offer their service to end customers directly and through partnerships with large banks. Since Blackrock’s significant investment in the company in 2015, they partner with Scalable to sell and license Scalable’s technology to their client base. With more than €2bn Assets Under Management, the company is Europe’s leading automated investment platform. They are on the way to revolutionize the fintech market, further with the launch of their broker business in 2020.
cards.list_description: Scalable Capital is a full-service online wealth manager for long term systematic wealth creation. It offers intelligent and cost-efficient investment and risk management technology that was commonly only available to large institutional investors.
cards.future_perspectives: Scalable Capital’s mission is to provide a wide group of investors with access to an investment service which was previously reserved for the very wealthy. They provide a personalized, globally-diversified portfolio designed to create long-term wealth. To do this, they select the best and most cost-efficient Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), monitor and manage customers’ portfolios continuously with their proprietary risk management technology

cards.about: Scoutbee is transforming the lifeblood of many organizations – the ability to discover, analyze and collaborate with optimal suppliers. Their unique AI capability and intuitive platform empowers teams to build the most valuable relationships and drive maximum business value from procurement.
cards.quote: AS ONE OF OUR EARLIEST INVESTORS, HV HAS ADDED VALUE EVERY DAY SINCE. JAN AND THE TEAM SUPPORT US WITH BOTH STRATEGIC GUIDANCE AND PRACTICAL SUPPORT TO BUILD SCOUTBEE AS AN ORGANIZATION. IN PARTICULAR, HV IS HIGHLY ACCESSIBLE AND ENTREPRENEURIAL IN SPIRIT, REGULARLY PROPOSES MARKET OPPORTUNITIES TO US, AND ACTS TO BUILD OUR CONFIDENCE.
cards.founders_names:
Gregor Stühler
Prof. Christian Heinrich
Lee Galbraith
Fabian Heinrich
cards.how_it_started:
Founded in 2015 by purchasing, operations experts and German engineers, scoutbee aspired to simplify scouting suppliers. The aim then, as it is today, is to improve the transparency of the supplier network.

Scoutbee understands the complexities and the tedious, manual process in scouting and sourcing suppliers. They craved to provide more transparency and insights on suppliers, knowing that there was a better way.

They built a software as a service suite, powered by Artificial Intelligence, or AI, and Big Data to make it easy for people that need the right product to find the right supplier with the right product – in a couple of weeks…not a few months. That’s what they call it Smarter Supplier Discovery.
cards.list_description: scoutbee’s innovative suite of sourcing tools supports procurement departments in meeting their most difficult challenges. From supplier searching and onboarding, to tendering and market analysis.
cards.future_perspectives: Scoutbee’s mission is to apply breakthrough technology and intelligence to the procurement industry to connect the right companies from across the globe and forge better business relationships. Their vision is to improve the B2B buying process by empowering procurement leaders through Artificial Intelligence and Big Data so that they can develop tomorrow’s future, today.

content.text: Storyblok's mission is to deliver the best Content Management System that validates and prioritizes content management innovations and enables teams to deliver their content in a fast and reliable way while building the remote company.

Alex and Dom, two creative spirits with a shared passion for digital innovation, found themselves navigating the complexities of content management systems while working at an agency. They cherished the versatility these systems offered but couldn't help feeling something was missing — a headless CMS that not only catered to the technical agility developers crave but also provided the user-friendly experience marketers relish. Driven by a blend of inspiration and necessity, they embarked on a journey to create what would become a beacon in the digital landscape: the world's pioneering headless CMS designed to seamlessly unite developers and business users alike.

Meanwhile, nestled within the picturesque Austrian city of Linz — a place renowned for its delectable Linzer Torte, which boasts the oldest cake recipe known to the world — was an innovative startup that caught the eye of an HV Capital investment manager. In 2021, this Linz-based gem made waves by securing $8.5 million in Series A funding, earmarked for international growth and product refinement.

Over the course of a year, a genuine connection grew between HV Capital and the team at Storyblok. It was a relationship nurtured with mutual understanding, building a foundation of trust. When faced with a decision, as eight-term sheets lay sprawled before them, they chose HV Capital. It was a partnership not just of contracts and capital but of shared visions and aspirations, ready to propel Storyblok onto the global stage.

cards.list_description: Storyblok is a Headless Content Management System that works seamlessly for both developers and business users.

content.text: Storyblok’s growth narrative underscores a fundamental shift in how content is created, managed, and experienced across borders, making it a case study in remote collaboration and international scaling in the digital age. The team is a pioneering force, reshaping the content management landscape with its robust, remote-friendly platform. Their mission is simple yet transformative: Craft content with care once, then deploy it effortlessly anywhere—and everywhere—it’s needed. This ethos is at the core of Storyblok’s ambition to become the CMS of the 21st century, breaking down barriers and bringing a global community of creators closer together.

The company has not only scaled up its team in numbers and talent but also has seen its customer-created projects skyrocket to over 120,000 in 130 countries over the past two years. An impressive cadre of 74,000 developers and marketers now use Storyblok’s platform, each adding a thread to a rapidly expanding global tapestry. This expansion speaks to the underlying strength and adaptability of Storyblok’s offering—a platform that has not only weathered the challenges of rapid growth but also thrived amid them.

cards.about: Sennder is the leading digital European road freight forwarder. Founded in 2015, the team around David, Nico and Julius develops technology to connect shippers with small trucking companies.
cards.quote:
TO THIS DATE, HV HAS BEEN AN INTIMATE SPARRING PARTNER ON ALL THE TOPICS THAT ARISE WHEN SCALING A COMPANY FROM 30 TO 500 PEOPLE IN ONLY 2.5 YEARS.

I HIGHLY VALUE BOTH THEIR CLARITY AND EXPERIENCE ON ALL BUSINESS MATTERS, BUT ALSO AND SPECIFICALLY THEIR EXTREMELY PERSONAL SUPPORT IN GUIDING US AS FOUNDERS THROUGH A ONCE IN A LIFETIME JOURNEY.
cards.founders_names:
David Nothacker
Nicolaus Schefenacker
Julius Köhler
cards.how_it_started:
HV first met sennder in the early days of 2017 when the team started out with the idea to use empty bus cargo capacity from companies such as FlixBus to build a cost-efficient parcel network. After speaking to dozens of shippers and carriers, the team soon realized that the road freight opportunity is much bigger than that and pivoted to becoming a full road-freight forwarder in the end of 2017.

Using technology to connect large shippers with small carriers, sennder’s growth exploded within only a few months. This didn’t go unnoticed and HV joined the team’s extraordinary journey by leading the Series A in April 2018 together with our friends from Project A.

When HV first invested, the team was outgrowing a cohort of young digital road-freight forwarders set out to bring the German logistics industry into the 21st century. Over the course of the next 18 months or so, the team was able to successfully expand into new regions and build a European footprint.
cards.list_description: sennder is a digital freight forwarder in the road freight industry, building Europe's largest technology-enabled truck network.
cards.future_perspectives:
Utilizing data and technology, the team aims to push the logistics industry into the 21st century by building the operating system for the European road-freight market.

In 2020, sennder launched a JV with Poste Italiane in Italy and acquired both Uber Freight Europe as well as Everoad making it the undisputed #1 digital road-freight forwarder in Europe. Today, sennder manages over 40,000 trucks with offices in Germany, France, Poland, Spain and Italy ensuring transparency and efficiency within the procurement and distribution of cargo for shippers.

cards.about: SumUp enables merchants to process payments across a multitude of channels: at the Point of Sale, Online, or via contactless payment links. Launched in 2012, the company has since expanded to 31 countries, showing impressive growth. Today, hundreds of thousands of small businesses around the world rely on SumUp to get paid. Beyond the proprietary hardware, mobile and web apps, SumUp has gone on to develop a suite of APIs and SDKs for integrating payments into other apps and services.
cards.slogan: A better way to get paid.
cards.how_it_started: We are in the midst of becoming a cashless society. In order to facilitate this transition, SumUp has focussed on making cashless payments as easy and seamless as possible. In 2015 when the mPOS market was relatively nascent and fragmented, the shareholders of SumUp and HV’s former portfolio company, payleven, decided to join forces and pull its individual strength behind a single company. This proved to be the starting point for impressive growth over the next few years.
cards.list_description: SumUp is the leading mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) company in Europe. Our company vision is to become the first ever global card acceptance brand. Today hundreds of thousands of merchants accept card payments with SumUp in 31 countries.
cards.future_perspectives: Beyond scale and capturing additional markets, there is a vast opportunity to provide additional services to small merchants. SumUp’s mission is to enable small business owners, providing them with the right tools and products to meet their objectives.

cards.about: Tourlane is Europe’s fastest-growing planning and booking service for expert-made dream vacations. The company combines proprietary technology with the knowledge of specialized travel experts for a seamless booking experience. It allows travelers to affordably plan and book personalized, multi-day trips online to over 50 destinations. Convenient and simple, it removes the hassle of coordinating and booking specialty travel from various operators. Tourlane raised $81 million in funding from some of the industry's most renowned venture capital firms: HV, Sequoia Capital, Spark Capital and DN Capital. They are rapidly expanding, offering multi-language service in several markets across Europe.
cards.quote:
A TRIP IS A PUZZLE, AND ON A PERFECT TRIP, ALL THE PIECES FIT TOGETHER SEAMLESSLY. OUR TECHNOLOGY ALLOWS US TO BUILD THESE COMPLEX ITINERARIES WITH EASE.

WE’VE MADE A NEW EXPERIENCE IN TRAVEL USING TECHNOLOGY AND TRAVEL EXPERTISE. CUSTOMIZING VACATIONS PUTS MEANING BACK INTO TRAVEL.
cards.how_it_started:
Julian Weselek and Julian Stiefel (“The Julians”), founded Tourlane in 2016 to shake up the industry. Seeing opportunity in the fragmented marketplace of individual travel they decided to create the ‘first global virtual travel agency’.

The Julians and Christian Saller from HV first met in 2016, after being introduced by common friends. Both sides immediately clicked: Christian had finally found the right team to back in the massive individual travel market, at which he had looked for some time. And the Julians were happy to have found a partner with deep expertise and insight in the travel sector. Tourlane and HV have been working successfully together since then, with Christian acting as chairman of the Tourlane board.
cards.list_description: Tourlane matches travellers with the best and most qualified travel specialists. Tourlane’s specialists provide individual guidance and travel planning, in order to offer travellers the perfectly customized package.
cards.future_perspectives: With a completely new take on planning and booking vacations, Tourlane aims to become the world’s largest provider of individual travel. Leveraging technology and employee expertise customers get exceptional value for once-in-a-lifetime trips.

cards.about: Upvest allows financial platforms to easily offer digital securities to retail investors. This saves them money in issuance and custody, compared to traditional banking.
cards.quote:
WE CONSIDER HV CAPITAL MORE THAN OUR INVESTORS. IT’S A GENUINE LONG-TERM PARTNERSHIP IN WHICH WE’VE FOUND EXPERIENCED ADVICE AND SUPPORT.

WE RECOGNIZED INSTANTLY THEY SHARED OUR AMBITION AND VISION, MAKING THEM THE IDEAL PARTNER TO ACHIEVE OUR GOALS
cards.slogan: The securities API for financial institutions.
cards.founders_names:
Martin Kassing
Ivan Mozorov
Jesper Noehr

content.text: HV invested in Upvest in 2017, when a small team of three was sharing an office in the attic above the Factory. HV was excited to back a team of extremely solid entrepreneurs with a strong background in building products for the fintech world. But it would take almost a year for the first product to launch.

The first idea was to create a platform for ICOs – which didn’t work out, but a lot of the technology created at the time turned into what Upvest is today! At HV we strongly believe in the recalibration of the traditional, centralized banking system into a more decentralized, blockchain-based future.

cards.list_description: Upvest’s blockchain APIs enable businesses to offer seamless blockchain wallets, transactions, smart contracts and data to their end users (B2B2C model). Upvest empowers anyone to access major blockchains like Bitcoin and Ethereum instantly without prior knowledge. One of the first use cases is fintechs and blockchain apps where the Upvest wallet infrastructure can be integrated as a self-custody solution with recovery features for the end-users, thereby replacing an intermediary bank.
cards.future_perspectives:
The long-term goal is building a more open and inclusive ecosystem to build amazing fintech applications. Upvest’s challenge is not only building easy-to-use blockchain APIs, but rather a product which needs to fit the regulatory environment, without sacrificing on security or user experience. First, the focus will first be on making existing services as reliable and scalable as possible before extending the solution in the dimensions of tech, security, and legal.

Upvest exists to open up the financial world providing economic opportunities for all. Our goal is to make securities globally available, allowing any asset to be owned and traded digitally by anyone, anywhere.

cards.about: Urban Sports Club is Europe’s leading sports and fitness platform. The company offers a flexible sports flat rate and connects partners with private and corporate customers. From fitness, yoga, swimming and climbing to team sports and wellness offers - members can choose from over 50 types of sport to create their own unique training plan and discover new activities. With over 12,000 partner locations in seven countries in Europe (Germany, Netherlands, France, Spain, Italy, Belgium and Portugal), members can check-in for sports via the app. Private and corporate customers can choose to train in studios, outdoors or online via livestream.
cards.quote:
WE ARE PARTNERS AND HAVE ALWAYS FELT THE SUPPORT ALONG THE WAY.

ESPECIALLY DURING DIFFICULT TIMES SUCH AS THE COVID-CRISIS
cards.slogan: Changing the way to discover the sport you love.
cards.how_it_started:
Moritz Kreppel, co-founder of Urban Sports Club, already knew Nawid Ali-Abbassi from HV Capital from the Berlin start-up scene. When HV Capital first met Moritz and his co-founder, Benjamin Roth, Urban Sports Club was an early-stage start-up. Their dream was to create a platform which would allow members to discover and do any type of sport at any time without borders across many European countries.

Moritz and Benjamin had created a new way of working out, exploring and finding new types of sport and studios. As a full-service provider for partners they wanted to let studios focus on what they love most: sports. They were about to prove that they would become Europe’s largest sports community. When Urban Sports Club acquired their competitor Somuchmore in 2016, David Kuczek became their partner and lead investor.

Nowadays, working out with Urban Sports Club has become the new status quo. Moritz Kreppel and Benjamin Roth founded Urban Sports Club in Berlin, Germany, in 2012. After two years of bootstrapping, the company secured early-stage financing in 2015 and went on to acquire other competitors across Europe. OneFit joined the Urban Sports Club family in August of 2019. Now, the Urban Sports Club network has more than 12,000 partners in six countries. Private and corporate customers can choose to train in studios, outdoors or online via livestream.

More than 400 employees work for the company. Urban Sports Club employs over 40 different nationalities in several locations across Europe. Moritz and Benjamin are still the CEOs of the company, actively managing day-to-day operations. They have also become business angels and mentors for other start-ups.
cards.future_perspectives: Urban Sport Club’s aim is to enable people to lead active and healthy lives. By providing the platform and technology, Urban Sports Club inspires people to continuously discover all sports they love. The company’s vision is a world where everyone enjoys doing sports.

content.quote: I HOPE I CAN BE A PARTNER AND RESOURCE TO THE FOUNDER, ESPECIALLY WHEN THE GOING GETS TOUGH – WHICH IT ALWAYS DOES.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

Growing up in the border triangle of Germany, France, and Switzerland, specifically in Lörrach, Maxi knew as a kid that her life would take place in a major city. In her formative years, Maxi immersed herself in sports, with pole vaulting as her athletic passion, and the world of art. At 17, Maxi embarked on a solo adventure, relocating to the vibrant

city of London. There, she learned how complicated things can get for a teenager to open a banking account or sign a lease. Her initial aspiration was to pursue a degree in Art and Design. Still, her new exposure to business and political leaders led her to switch gears and delve into Management.

Maxi's academic journey has been remarkable and equipped her with a wealth of knowledge and a global perspective. She earned her Bachelor's degree in Management at the prestigious London School of Economics. Her quest for knowledge then took her to Tsinghua University as a Schwarzman Scholar, specializing in technology and entrepreneurship in China. Her academic pursuits reached their zenith at Harvard Business School, where she achieved the coveted title of Baker Scholar. Diversity and equity are more than just buzzwords for Maxi. She has led this realm, from leading the German delegation to the G7 Youth Summit in 2017 to steering initiatives such as the Women in Investing conference and a women’s angel group with a mission to increase women's presence on cap tables at Harvard Business School.

Before stints with US-based venture and PE funds during her MBA, Maxi spent three years at the McKinsey Berlin office, where she built digital products and services in healthcare and e-government in Europe. Her contributions extended to the McKinsey Global Institute in San Francisco, where she served as the annual tech and innovation fellow in 2019. Her work on the Bio Revolution report delved into the convergence of innovation in life science and digital technologies. Fuelled by her interactions with the
vibrant
Silicon Valley ecosystem, Maxi relaunched and led McKinsey’s Fuel Ignition startup initiative in Berlin.

Outside of work, Sci-fi books and art galleries captivate Maxi’s imagination, while yoga and outdoor adventures like climbing Kilimanjaro keep her balanced. Now, Maxi's role at HV Capital positions her as a driving force in shaping the future of early-stage investments: she seeks out new technologies that advance society and founders who never give up in their quest to build great, lasting companies.

content.quote:
I LIKE THE IMPACT THAT A VC CAN HAVE, IT IS SIMILAR TO A TRAINER. IF YOU GAIN THE TRUST OF THE FOUNDERS, YOU CAN REACH MIGHTY THINGS TOGETHER.

FOR THIS YOU HAVE TO BE CLEAR, DETERMINED, FLEXIBLE AND CONNECTED.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.quote:
TALKING TO FOUNDERS, I REALIZE THAT WE HAVE JUST SCRATCHED THE SURFACE OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH TECHNOLOGY.

HOW COULD YOU NOT BE INSPIRED KNOWING THAT YOU ARE SURROUNDED BY THE GREATEST MINDS IN THEIR RESPECTIVE FIELDS?

content.text: Being born in flight, living in refugee houses, and seeing his parents start from scratch over and over again shaped Said from an early age. His parents set an example of what entrepreneurship means: having the guts and perseverance to challenge the status quo for a better tomorrow, against all odds.

Said holds degrees in Economics and Business Administration. He undertook his studies at Goethe University Frankfurt and Wharton Business School, experiencing the vivid east coast start-up ecosystem while at the latter. Inspired, he started his entrepreneurial career as the first intern in HV's then newly opened Berlin office.

Being exposed to so much knowledge in a concentrated period, Said put the lessons he learned into action. He joined a start-up as their CFO to help build the long-stay marketplace for business travellers. He was responsible for two financing rounds, gaining first-hand experience of fundraising and the emotional rollercoaster of founding a company.

Said found walking in the shoes of an entrepreneur a very humbling experience, with extreme ups and downs. It also helps him connect with other founders "beyond the pitch." When founders show passion and hustle, they will often win his support.

Said's fear of missing out on the next tech endeavor brought him to Venture Capital, where he can quench his thirst for tech-enabled improvements across different industries. When he is not reading and talking tech, Said is likely looking for the next fitness and longevity trend to try out, or watching live techno sets to kickstart his long-postponed DJ career.

Born and raised in the Western part of Germany, Frederic grew up in a family that have been entrepreneurs since the 1860s, teaching him the importance of having clear values and long-term orientation.

Frederic studied International Business Administration at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management with an exchange at IE University in Madrid and then pursued his Master degree in Management and Technology at The Technical University of Munich while simultaneously graduating from the Honours Degree in Technology Management at the Center for Digital Technology and Management in Munich.

Being fascinated by the potential of the intersection of entrepreneurship and technology, Frederic first joined the extended HV family as an intern at HV's portfolio company Wellster Healthtech Group followed by a short stint at Picus Capital. Afterwards, Frederic joined HV’s early stage investment team in 2020 as an intern. Frederic then went on to continue as a working student, with a short stint at McKinsey & Company, before joining HV full-time in 2022.

Frederic loves spending his free time on a sailing boat in summer and skiing in the mountains in winter. Frederic also tries to improve his tennis skills and can be  occasionally found on Berlin and Munich’s paddle courts. Furthermore, he enjoys spending time with friends over dinner and a glass of wine.

content.text: Fabian's passion for understanding complex systems and concepts stems from his upbringing, influenced by his mother, a computer scientist, and his father, an engineer. This early exposure ignited his curiosity about harnessing technology to tackle hard challenges.

He also holds a degree in Technology Management from the CDTM in Munich and Columbia Business School in New York. His career began at BCG and J.P. Morgan, advising technology companies, followed by his first experience in venture capital at Munich-based growth fund Acton Capital.

As employee #1 and initial CMO/CRO at Foodora, Fabian spearheaded one of Europe's fastest growing venture scale-ups, growing the company from a single employee (himself) to hundreds in just months.  He built global sales and marketing teams from the ground up, demonstrating his strategic and operational expertise.

Since joining HV in early 2018, Fabian has  shifted his focus towards DeepTech and growth investments, particularly in Series B and beyond. His portfolio includes pioneering hardware DeepTech companies like Isar Aerospace, Neura Robotics, and Quantum Systems, as well as cutting-edge enterprise software firms such as Flip, Spread.ai, and OneData. Fabian’s analytical focus and strong network make him a valuable partner to ambitious founders on their quest to solve complex challenges to potentially change the world.
Now residing in Berlin, Fabian enjoys cycling around the city’s picturesque lakes, balancing his professional life with a passion for exploring the outdoors.

content.text: What makes Kipu unique is the focus on application- and hardware-specific quantum algorithms that are packaged into software products. Kipu operates at the nexus of customer use cases, hardware platforms, and the software layer – because quantum computers are still more than 10 years away from solving meaningful problems with standard approaches. The team intends to drastically reduce the time to useful quantum computing.

content.quote:
YOU HAVE TO START BEFORE YOU ARE READY. ENTREPRENEURSHIP IS ABOUT MOVING FAST, LEARNING AND ADAPTING CONTINUOUSLY, RATHER THAN STRIVING FOR PERFECTION.

THINK BIG AND ASK YOURSELF WHAT WOULD BE THE BOLDER VERSION OF YOUR NEXT MOVE.

content.text: Laura was born in the US, grew up in Germany and moved to Switzerland as a teenager. She studied in Hamburg, London and Paris, obtained her PhD in Finance at the University of St. Gallen and conducted research at Columbia University, New York. Her global experience ensures that Laura always brings a broad perspective to her work in VC.

After a stint in the VC world at Headline, Laura worked at J.P. Morgan on various corporate finance transactions – mostly across TMT and consumer industries, including IPOs, financings, buy- and sell-side mandates. Taking a more entrepreneurial approach, Laura co-founded WeSpace, the first work and community space designed for female professionals in the DACH region, for which she earned Forbes "30 Under 30" recognition.
At HV, Laura is part of the venture team where she seeks out promising startups across industries with a particular focus on healthcare and techbio.

In venture capital, Laura states money is not the differentiating factor, but rather the people who are behind the money. Partnering with seasoned investors is key - particularly when developing large, sustainable companies.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.text: Alexander discovered his passion for investing early on, making his first stock trade at the age of 14 from his one-year pocket money savings. While still in high-school, admittedly missing a class or two, he started building up a portfolio of stocks with an affinity for tech-driven companies. Only to lose it all in the dot-com bubble in 2000. Having been burnt from investing, he re-focused on his education: He pursued a Bachelor and two Master degrees from EBS and the University of Cambridge, graduating top of his class and being awarded various scholarships and prizes such as DAAD and Student of the Year.

Alexander started his professional career at Morgan Stanley's investment banking team amid the challenging times of the financial crisis. Being a stickler for loyalty, he stayed at the bank for nearly a decade in different roles and locations, deal captaining executions of a variety of banking products within M&A and capital markets such as IPOs, equity, debt and derivatives.

Afterwards and with his experience from MS, he supported Delivery Hero in its successful IPO in 2017 and jointly helped turn it into a DAX company, leading its M&A and VC efforts as Head and Group VP, and also being responsible for all of its corporate finance activities. This included >20 investments in growth companies with a total AuM of nearly EUR 1 billion, including successfully picking several unicorns and decacorns, among others, Glovo, Rappi, Zomato, Impossible Food, EatJust, Ola and Instashop as well as other cross-vertical investments in the FinTech, B2B SaaS, FoodTech and ESG space.

Through his bi-cultural background from living in Berlin and Bogotá, both two very divergent cultures, he feels incredibly lucky having learnt to appreciate the diversity of people's behaviour and perspective – not always picking up the best virtues of each culture, he admits.

He always had a passion for products with the ability to fundamentally change consumer behaviour such as last-mile logistics, scalable marketplaces, alternative protein or ESG in general. Given his role in co-leading the Growth Team at HV, however, he predominantly looks for sector-agnostic criteria in passionate and ambitious founders.
In
his spare time, Alexander enjoys traveling, street art and Italian wine. But mostly he likes sports, anything competitive, preferably with any type of racket.

Born and raised in a small village called Gülzow, Jannis spent his early days playing and coaching the local soccer and tennis teams. A fortunate coincidence landed his 16-year-old self in a 4-week internship at a Berlin-based ticketing startup. The experience of leaving his hometown and spending a month in Germany's startup capital sparked his enthusiasm for entrepreneurship and tech at a young age. Jannis then decided to pursue this interest further at WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, where he later earned his bachelor's degree. From day one of his enrolment, Jannis worked hard to gain a foothold in the German startup ecosystem. To that end, he took part in multiple entrepreneurial initiatives and projects throughout his time at WHU.

Jannis started his professional career at the HV portfolio company Scalable Capital during the pre-product stage. Following his stint there, he went on to join the team of Hello Fresh in New York to work on optimizing their procurement strategies. After getting to know the operational side of a very young startup in high-growth mode, Jannis joined the investment world. After two initial internships at Headline and Index Ventures, he started as an investment analyst for Lakestar.

He contributed to several notable early- and growth-stage deals across Europe and had his first touchpoints with the HV Capital team. In February 2021, Jannis became an Associate for the Growth Team at HV Capital.

Looking back, Janis says: "Humility, proactive helpfulness, and gratitude have been the most important lessons I've learned in my career so far, and I believe these qualities are important at every stage of life."

Jannis perceives the daily work of a VC as one of the most encouraging and challenging things he has ever done: "Daily, you discuss new technologies, business models, and markets with a very nimble group of founders and colleagues."
During his free time, Jannis spends his time kitesurfing, playing tennis, and organizing short trips and events for his friends and family.

Born and raised in rural Austria, Jakob developed an early passion for computers and understanding how they work. Experimenting with a Windows Me machine, he built his own text-based pocket monster game before he was a teenager but could never quite figure out how to add the graphics. Supporting incredibly talented entrepreneurs on their journey of developing products that transform our work and lives is what has drawn him into VC.

Growing up, Jakob spent most of his time in basketball gyms across Austria and beyond. As the dream of playing in the NBA failed to materialize, Jakob subsequently completed bachelor's and master's programs at WU Vienna and HSG, respectively, and studied abroad in Canada, the US and China.

Before joining HV, Jakob co-founded a foodtech venture during the height of the first Covid-19 wave. After selling it, he worked in Private Equity at Goldman Sachs in London, focusing on late-stage investments across Europe.
Jakob loves spending his free time in the Austrian alps, trying out new sports and is far too passionate about his AeroPress. He still hasn't lost hope that he will write half-decent code one day.

content.text: Over the span of two decades, Kinnevik and HV Capital have meticulously crafted a partnership rooted in trust and mutual respect. Their collaborative efforts have been instrumental in the ascendancy of eminent brands including Zalando, Delivery Hero, and Home24. In the nascent stages of their partnership, Climate Tech remained peripheral. However, as the European ecosystem matured, echoing the global shift towards sustainability, Climate Tech transformed into a point of strategic interest.

At HV Capital Alex and Jannis, whose exploided for two years the Climate Tech landscape before discovering Agreena. Hailing from the fertile innovation soil of Copenhagen, Agreena stood at the crossroads of Climate Tech, Fintech, and Agtech, showcasing a multi-faceted approach to environmental solutions. Kinnevik, as one of the early believers in Agreena's vision, laid the foundational trust that would subsequently be built upon. With a rich reservoir of in-house expertise and the catalytic influence of the enduring partnership with Kinnevik, HV Capital emerged not just as investors but as trusted allies to Agreena's founding trio - Julie Koch Fahler, Ida Boesen, and Simon Haldrup.

Leading Agreena's Series B funding round with investors like Giant Ventures, re:Food, Aenu, and Vaeksfonden was more than a financial endeavor for HV Capital; it was a forward leap into a future where technology and climate coalesce into solutions that transcend contemporary boundaries and redefine sustainable innovation.

Agreena stands at the forefront of a global movement, pioneering a carbon farming platform that is not just innovative but transformative, serving farmers worldwide in their transition to regenerative agriculture. In a world where agriculture is a significant contributor to greenhouse gas emissions, Agreena emerges as a beacon of change, illuminating pathways where agriculture transforms from a challenge to a solution.

By bridging Climate Tech with Fintech and Agtech, Agreena catalyzes a global adoption of sustainable practices through its financial reward schemes, offering tangible incentives for ecological farming transitions. Beyond its financial mechanisms, Agreena carries a deeper vision – to sow the seeds for a future where farming nourishes a planet abundant in biodiversity, food safety, sustainability, and health, with technology as the cornerstone of this green revolution.

The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

Nikolas grew up on the countryside south of Hamburg. After school he travelled around the world with his two best friends, visiting Thailand, Cambodia, Australia, New Zealand, Argentina, Uruguay and Cuba. In Australia, he became a driver for the recently launched food delivery service Deliveroo, where he worked his way up to a role in the operations team. After that, Nikolas caught the startup bug and interned at another food delivery startup in Hamburg called Stadtsalat.

Nikolas studied Business Administration at WWU in Münster – a great challenge for him, not coming from an academic household. During his exchange semester in Guadalajara, Mexico, he spent time learning Spanish. After a couple of internships, Nikolas caught the crypto bug in 2017 and bought his first crypto (bitcoin and Ethereum) before writing his bachelor’s thesis on the disruptiveness of stable coins and crypto in general.

Seeking a career in crypto, Nikolas began writing articles on new DeFi projects to build his network and reputation, before landing a job at a small crypto fund in Hamburg. Next, he moved to Lisbon to study a Master of Business at Nova SBE. At the end of his studies, Nikolas began a crypto internship with HV Capital in Berlin, where he now works full time as an Analyst with a focus on the crypto space.

Nikolas is a family person and loves to be around his family. In his free time, he loves to read, cook, travel, play sports and enjoy being in nature. He is also a passionate vegetarian, stemming from his love of nature and animals.

TALKING TO FOUNDERS, I REALIZE THAT WE HAVE JUST SCRATCHED THE SURFACE OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH TECHNOLOGY.

content.text: Being born in flight, living in refugee houses, and seeing his parents start from scratch over and over again shaped Said from an early age. His parents set an example of what entrepreneurship means: having the guts and perseverance to challenge the status quo for a better tomorrow, against all odds.

Said holds degrees in Economics and Business Administration. He undertook his studies at Goethe University Frankfurt and Wharton Business School, experiencing the vivid east coast start-up ecosystem while at the latter. Inspired, he started his entrepreneurial career as the first intern in HV's then newly opened Berlin office.

Being exposed to so much knowledge in a concentrated period, Said put the lessons he learned into action. He joined a start-up as their CFO to help build the long-stay marketplace for business travellers. He was responsible for two financing rounds, gaining first-hand experience of fundraising and the emotional rollercoaster of founding a company.

Said found walking in the shoes of an entrepreneur a very humbling experience, with extreme ups and downs. It also helps him connect with other founders "beyond the pitch." When founders show passion and hustle, they will often win his support.

Said's fear of missing out on the next tech endeavor brought him to Venture Capital, where he can quench his thirst for tech-enabled improvements across different industries. When he is not reading and talking tech, Said is likely looking for the next fitness and longevity trend to try out, or watching live techno sets to kickstart his long-postponed DJ career.

Born and raised in the Western part of Germany, Frederic grew up in a family that have been entrepreneurs since the 1860s, teaching him the importance of having clear values and long-term orientation.

Frederic studied International Business Administration at WHU – Otto Beisheim School of Management with an exchange at IE University in Madrid and then pursued his Master degree in Management and Technology at The Technical University of Munich while simultaneously graduating from the Honours Degree in Technology Management at the Center for Digital Technology and Management in Munich.

Being fascinated by the potential of the intersection of entrepreneurship and technology, Frederic first joined the extended HV family as an intern at HV's portfolio company Wellster Healthtech Group followed by a short stint at Picus Capital. Afterwards, Frederic joined HV’s early stage investment team in 2020 as an intern. Frederic then went on to continue as a working student, with a short stint at McKinsey & Company, before joining HV full-time in 2022.

Frederic loves spending his free time on a sailing boat in summer and skiing in the mountains in winter. Frederic also tries to improve his tennis skills and can be  occasionally found on Berlin and Munich’s paddle courts. Furthermore, he enjoys spending time with friends over dinner and a glass of wine.
