content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

Growing up in a small town in the Polish mountains, Zuzanna has always been curious to discover the world. Her determination and enthusiasm have led her to earn a Bachelor's degree in International Business at Rotterdam School of Management. She also completed a Master's Degree in Finance at Esade Business School in Barcelona. Having lived in the Netherlands, United States, Kenya, Spain, United Kingdom, and Germany and hiking to the most remote locations globally, she developed a strong appreciation for different people, cultures, and the diverse ways we experience the world. On a professional level, her desire to explore multiple paths ultimately led her to gather experiences across organizations such as NGOs, early-stage ventures, and large corporates worldwide.

She started her professional career in a start-up in Nairobi, Kenya, where she learned that the life of a founder is filled with constant ups & downs. Similarly, she developed a genuine appreciation for big ideas, the complexity of running a business, and the power of teamwork.

Before joining HV, Zuzanna spent two years in private debt and private equity at BlackRock in London. Here she focused on climate tech and renewable power investments across Europe and gained hands-on deal experience. She developed a strong commitment to working towards a better future and embraced the spirit of being a lifelong student of technology, markets, and the world. At Goldman Sachs and Global Founders Capital, she gained valuable know-how in investment banking and venture capital.
At HV Capital, Zuzanna focuses on Fintech & B2B SaaS.

Discussing disruptive ideas and meeting founders with an ambition to challenge how we live our everyday lives or run businesses across the globe are the things that excite her most. She loves supporting extraordinary visions, building long-lasting relationships, and helping others solve complex problems.
In her spare time, you will most likely find Zuzanna hiking in the mountains, reading the next best-seller, or cooking for friends & family.

content.text: Alexander discovered his passion for investing early on, making his first stock trade at the age of 14 from his one-year pocket money savings. While still in high-school, admittedly missing a class or two, he started building up a portfolio of stocks with an affinity for tech-driven companies. Only to lose it all in the dot-com bubble in 2000. Having been burnt from investing, he re-focused on his education: He pursued a Bachelor and two Master degrees from EBS and the University of Cambridge, graduating top of his class and being awarded various scholarships and prizes such as DAAD and Student of the Year.

Alexander started his professional career at Morgan Stanley's investment banking team amid the challenging times of the financial crisis. Being a stickler for loyalty, he stayed at the bank for nearly a decade in different roles and locations, deal captaining executions of a variety of banking products within M&A and capital markets such as IPOs, equity, debt and derivatives.

Afterwards and with his experience from MS, he supported Delivery Hero in its successful IPO in 2017 and jointly helped turn it into a DAX company, leading its M&A and VC efforts as Head and Group VP, and also being responsible for all of its corporate finance activities. This included >20 investments in growth companies with a total AuM of nearly EUR 1 billion, including successfully picking several unicorns and decacorns, among others, Glovo, Rappi, Zomato, Impossible Food, EatJust, Ola and Instashop as well as other cross-vertical investments in the FinTech, B2B SaaS, FoodTech and ESG space.

Through his bi-cultural background from living in Berlin and Bogotá, both two very divergent cultures, he feels incredibly lucky having learnt to appreciate the diversity of people's behaviour and perspective – not always picking up the best virtues of each culture, he admits.

He always had a passion for products with the ability to fundamentally change consumer behaviour such as last-mile logistics, scalable marketplaces, alternative protein or ESG in general. Given his role in co-leading the Growth Team at HV, however, he predominantly looks for sector-agnostic criteria in passionate and ambitious founders.
In
his spare time, Alexander enjoys traveling, street art and Italian wine. But mostly he likes sports, anything competitive, preferably with any type of racket.

Born and raised in a small village called Gülzow, Jannis spent his early days playing and coaching the local soccer and tennis teams. A fortunate coincidence landed his 16-year-old self in a 4-week internship at a Berlin-based ticketing startup. The experience of leaving his hometown and spending a month in Germany's startup capital sparked his enthusiasm for entrepreneurship and tech at a young age. Jannis then decided to pursue this interest further at WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, where he later earned his bachelor's degree. From day one of his enrolment, Jannis worked hard to gain a foothold in the German startup ecosystem. To that end, he took part in multiple entrepreneurial initiatives and projects throughout his time at WHU.

Jannis started his professional career at the HV portfolio company Scalable Capital during the pre-product stage. Following his stint there, he went on to join the team of Hello Fresh in New York to work on optimizing their procurement strategies. After getting to know the operational side of a very young startup in high-growth mode, Jannis joined the investment world. After two initial internships at Headline and Index Ventures, he started as an investment analyst for Lakestar.

He contributed to several notable early- and growth-stage deals across Europe and had his first touchpoints with the HV Capital team. In February 2021, Jannis became an Associate for the Growth Team at HV Capital.

Looking back, Janis says: "Humility, proactive helpfulness, and gratitude have been the most important lessons I've learned in my career so far, and I believe these qualities are important at every stage of life."

Jannis perceives the daily work of a VC as one of the most encouraging and challenging things he has ever done: "Daily, you discuss new technologies, business models, and markets with a very nimble group of founders and colleagues."
During his free time, Jannis spends his time kitesurfing, playing tennis, and organizing short trips and events for his friends and family.

Alex and Dom, two creative spirits with a shared passion for digital innovation, found themselves navigating the complexities of content management systems while working at an agency. They cherished the versatility these systems offered but couldn't help feeling something was missing — a headless CMS that not only catered to the technical agility developers crave but also provided the user-friendly experience marketers relish. Driven by a blend of inspiration and necessity, they embarked on a journey to create what would become a beacon in the digital landscape: the world's pioneering headless CMS designed to seamlessly unite developers and business users alike.

Meanwhile, nestled within the picturesque Austrian city of Linz — a place renowned for its delectable Linzer Torte, which boasts the oldest cake recipe known to the world — was an innovative startup that caught the eye of an HV Capital investment manager. In 2021, this Linz-based gem made waves by securing $8.5 million in Series A funding, earmarked for international growth and product refinement.

Over the course of a year, a genuine connection grew between HV Capital and the team at Storyblok. It was a relationship nurtured with mutual understanding, building a foundation of trust. When faced with a decision, as eight-term sheets lay sprawled before them, they chose HV Capital. It was a partnership not just of contracts and capital but of shared visions and aspirations, ready to propel Storyblok onto the global stage.

content.list_description: Storyblok is a Headless Content Management System that works seamlessly for both developers and business users.

content.text: Storyblok’s growth narrative underscores a fundamental shift in how content is created, managed, and experienced across borders, making it a case study in remote collaboration and international scaling in the digital age. The team is a pioneering force, reshaping the content management landscape with its robust, remote-friendly platform. Their mission is simple yet transformative: Craft content with care once, then deploy it effortlessly anywhere—and everywhere—it’s needed. This ethos is at the core of Storyblok’s ambition to become the CMS of the 21st century, breaking down barriers and bringing a global community of creators closer together.

The company has not only scaled up its team in numbers and talent but also has seen its customer-created projects skyrocket to over 120,000 in 130 countries over the past two years. An impressive cadre of 74,000 developers and marketers now use Storyblok’s platform, each adding a thread to a rapidly expanding global tapestry. This expansion speaks to the underlying strength and adaptability of Storyblok’s offering—a platform that has not only weathered the challenges of rapid growth but also thrived amid them.

AND ONCE CONVINCED, I AM SURE ALL OF US AT HV WOULD BEG, BORROW AND STEAL TO HELP REACH HER GOALS.

content.text: Alexander discovered his passion for investing early on, making his first stock trade at the age of 14 from his one-year pocket money savings. While still in high-school, admittedly missing a class or two, he started building up a portfolio of stocks with an affinity for tech-driven companies. Only to lose it all in the dot-com bubble in 2000. Having been burnt from investing, he re-focused on his education: He pursued a Bachelor and two Master degrees from EBS and the University of Cambridge, graduating top of his class and being awarded various scholarships and prizes such as DAAD and Student of the Year.

Alexander started his professional career at Morgan Stanley's investment banking team amid the challenging times of the financial crisis. Being a stickler for loyalty, he stayed at the bank for nearly a decade in different roles and locations, deal captaining executions of a variety of banking products within M&A and capital markets such as IPOs, equity, debt and derivatives.

Afterwards and with his experience from MS, he supported Delivery Hero in its successful IPO in 2017 and jointly helped turn it into a DAX company, leading its M&A and VC efforts as Head and Group VP, and also being responsible for all of its corporate finance activities. This included >20 investments in growth companies with a total AuM of nearly EUR 1 billion, including successfully picking several unicorns and decacorns, among others, Glovo, Rappi, Zomato, Impossible Food, EatJust, Ola and Instashop as well as other cross-vertical investments in the FinTech, B2B SaaS, FoodTech and ESG space.

Through his bi-cultural background from living in Berlin and Bogotá, both two very divergent cultures, he feels incredibly lucky having learnt to appreciate the diversity of people's behaviour and perspective – not always picking up the best virtues of each culture, he admits.

He always had a passion for products with the ability to fundamentally change consumer behaviour such as last-mile logistics, scalable marketplaces, alternative protein or ESG in general. Given his role in co-leading the Growth Team at HV, however, he predominantly looks for sector-agnostic criteria in passionate and ambitious founders.
In
his spare time, Alexander enjoys traveling, street art and Italian wine. But mostly he likes sports, anything competitive, preferably with any type of racket.

Born and raised in a small village called Gülzow, Jannis spent his early days playing and coaching the local soccer and tennis teams. A fortunate coincidence landed his 16-year-old self in a 4-week internship at a Berlin-based ticketing startup. The experience of leaving his hometown and spending a month in Germany's startup capital sparked his enthusiasm for entrepreneurship and tech at a young age. Jannis then decided to pursue this interest further at WHU - Otto Beisheim School of Management, where he later earned his bachelor's degree. From day one of his enrolment, Jannis worked hard to gain a foothold in the German startup ecosystem. To that end, he took part in multiple entrepreneurial initiatives and projects throughout his time at WHU.

Jannis started his professional career at the HV portfolio company Scalable Capital during the pre-product stage. Following his stint there, he went on to join the team of Hello Fresh in New York to work on optimizing their procurement strategies. After getting to know the operational side of a very young startup in high-growth mode, Jannis joined the investment world. After two initial internships at Headline and Index Ventures, he started as an investment analyst for Lakestar.

He contributed to several notable early- and growth-stage deals across Europe and had his first touchpoints with the HV Capital team. In February 2021, Jannis became an Associate for the Growth Team at HV Capital.

Looking back, Janis says: "Humility, proactive helpfulness, and gratitude have been the most important lessons I've learned in my career so far, and I believe these qualities are important at every stage of life."

Jannis perceives the daily work of a VC as one of the most encouraging and challenging things he has ever done: "Daily, you discuss new technologies, business models, and markets with a very nimble group of founders and colleagues."
During his free time, Jannis spends his time kitesurfing, playing tennis, and organizing short trips and events for his friends and family.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

Susie's curiosity about the world has always been the baseline for her every move: It has taken her from a small Bavarian town to Spain, the US, China, the UK and Munich. It has led her from studying Business Administration to courses in Mathematics, Psychology, American Politics, and Finance. It allowed her to find food for thought in scholarship programmes, while pushing the boundaries of her adrenaline levels by running marathons and skydiving in Hawaii. On a professional level, her curiosity enabled her to experience a whole range of work environments, from NGOs to large blue-chip companies to mid-market companies to early-stage ventures.

Susie moved to the UK in 2014 to pursue a MSc in Finance and Private Equity from the LSE and ended up spending 7 years in London, before moving back to Munich. Working in investment banking taught her much more than just quantitative modelling skills – it taught her structure, diligence and self-discipline. It also enabled her to immerse herself in a wide variety of industries, solve complex challenges and understand the anatomy of successful global companies. But it was the world of scale-ups and start-ups that ultimately won her heart.

The pivotal moment happened in 2018, while working on a year-long project with one of the fastest-growing tech scale-ups in the UK. The combination of a highly dynamic team, a lightspeed uptick in customer numbers, a true hyper-growth momentum, a seemingly never-ending need to hire across an entire organisation and to close new funding rounds felt energising on every level. The immense thrill of the moment made her fall in love with early-stage software companies and unlocked the door to investing for her.

At HV Capital, Susie works as a Principal covering FinTech and DeFi. The world of Venture allows her to combine all of her passions: to put her innate curiosity to work, while letting her creativity and big ideas run free. She takes energy from listening to founders who overcome the most difficult obstacles, while making it all look natural and effortless. She loves dissecting the competitive landscapes that visionary founders are disrupting. And she is obsessed with connecting people in the ecosystem that she believes could form great teams.

Growing up in a small town in the Polish mountains, Zuzanna has always been curious to discover the world. Her determination and enthusiasm have led her to earn a Bachelor's degree in International Business at Rotterdam School of Management. She also completed a Master's Degree in Finance at Esade Business School in Barcelona. Having lived in the Netherlands, United States, Kenya, Spain, United Kingdom, and Germany and hiking to the most remote locations globally, she developed a strong appreciation for different people, cultures, and the diverse ways we experience the world. On a professional level, her desire to explore multiple paths ultimately led her to gather experiences across organizations such as NGOs, early-stage ventures, and large corporates worldwide.

She started her professional career in a start-up in Nairobi, Kenya, where she learned that the life of a founder is filled with constant ups & downs. Similarly, she developed a genuine appreciation for big ideas, the complexity of running a business, and the power of teamwork.

Before joining HV, Zuzanna spent two years in private debt and private equity at BlackRock in London. Here she focused on climate tech and renewable power investments across Europe and gained hands-on deal experience. She developed a strong commitment to working towards a better future and embraced the spirit of being a lifelong student of technology, markets, and the world. At Goldman Sachs and Global Founders Capital, she gained valuable know-how in investment banking and venture capital.
At HV Capital, Zuzanna focuses on Fintech & B2B SaaS.

Discussing disruptive ideas and meeting founders with an ambition to challenge how we live our everyday lives or run businesses across the globe are the things that excite her most. She loves supporting extraordinary visions, building long-lasting relationships, and helping others solve complex problems.
In her spare time, you will most likely find Zuzanna hiking in the mountains, reading the next best-seller, or cooking for friends & family.

content.text: Felix is always seeking companies with big ambition and the drive to transform the European technology landscape. On a daily basis he reflects on the role of VC. He channels this awareness and responsibility towards his personal interactions with portfolios, entrepreneurs and teams.

Felix studied business and political science in Munich, Singapore and London. His educational background spans the complexity, nuances and fragility of international relations. Felix graduated with a BSc in Business Administration from LMU Munich with distinction. He completed his International Political Economy Masters with distinction at LSE London.

Prior to joining HV, Felix was CEO and co-founder of a VC-backed digital learning platform, helping to build and manage the platform. He suffered and celebrated while bringing mobile learning to higher education in Europe. The company eventually sold to a competitor, and then later to StepStone.

Felix enjoys both challenging and supporting founders in their most crucial moments. He holds onto the heart and soul that he and his co-founders put into their company 24/7 over many years. At HV he has worked on projects such as sennder, Dialogue, heartbeat and homefully.

In his spare time, Felix enjoys climbing (especially bouldering), both indoors and outdoors. He also loves almost any other type of sports, including tennis, soccer, badminton, squash and beach volleyball.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.quote: The thrill of venture capital lies in partnering with founders who push the boundaries of what's possible and figuring out how they can be supported to push just a little harder.

content.text: Fabian's passion for understanding complex systems and concepts stems from his upbringing, influenced by his mother, a computer scientist, and his father, an engineer. This early exposure ignited his curiosity about harnessing technology to tackle hard challenges.

Fabian studied Business Administration and Computer Science at WHU and TU Munich, consistently graduating at the top of his class. He also holds a degree in Technology Management from the CDTM in Munich and Columbia Business School in New York. His career began at BCG and J.P. Morgan, advising technology companies, followed by his first experience in venture capital at Munich-based growth fund Acton Capital.

As employee #1 and initial CMO/CRO at Foodora, Fabian spearheaded one of Europe's fastest growing venture scale-ups, growing the company from a single employee (himself) to hundreds in just months.  He built global sales and marketing teams from the ground up, demonstrating his strategic and operational expertise.

Since joining HV in early 2018, Fabian has  shifted his focus towards DeepTech and growth investments, particularly in Series B and beyond. His portfolio includes pioneering hardware DeepTech companies like Isar Aerospace, Neura Robotics, and Quantum Systems, as well as cutting-edge enterprise software firms such as Flip, Spread.ai, and OneData. Fabian’s analytical focus and strong network make him a valuable partner to ambitious founders on their quest to solve complex challenges to potentially change the world.
Now residing in Berlin, Fabian enjoys cycling around the city’s picturesque lakes, balancing his professional life with a passion for exploring the outdoors.

TALKING TO FOUNDERS, I REALIZE THAT WE HAVE JUST SCRATCHED THE SURFACE OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH TECHNOLOGY.

content.text: Being born in flight, living in refugee houses, and seeing his parents start from scratch over and over again shaped Said from an early age. His parents set an example of what entrepreneurship means: having the guts and perseverance to challenge the status quo for a better tomorrow, against all odds.

Said holds degrees in Economics and Business Administration. He undertook his studies at Goethe University Frankfurt and Wharton Business School, experiencing the vivid east coast start-up ecosystem while at the latter. Inspired, he started his entrepreneurial career as the first intern in HV's then newly opened Berlin office.

Being exposed to so much knowledge in a concentrated period, Said put the lessons he learned into action. He joined a start-up as their CFO to help build the long-stay marketplace for business travellers. He was responsible for two financing rounds, gaining first-hand experience of fundraising and the emotional rollercoaster of founding a company.

Said found walking in the shoes of an entrepreneur a very humbling experience, with extreme ups and downs. It also helps him connect with other founders "beyond the pitch." When founders show passion and hustle, they will often win his support.

Said's fear of missing out on the next tech endeavor brought him to Venture Capital, where he can quench his thirst for tech-enabled improvements across different industries. When he is not reading and talking tech, Said is likely looking for the next fitness and longevity trend to try out, or watching live techno sets to kickstart his long-postponed DJ career.

content.quote: THE BEAUTY OF TECHNOLOGICAL DISRUPTION IS THAT IT ENABLES ENTREPRENEURS TO THINK OUTSIDE OF EXISTING CONSTRAINTS AND SOLVE FOR AN OUTCOME THAT PROVIDES A GIANT LEAP FORWARD IN THE SECTOR THEY ARE IN.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

AND ONCE CONVINCED, I AM SURE ALL OF US AT HV WOULD BEG, BORROW AND STEAL TO HELP REACH HER GOALS.

content.text: Alexander discovered his passion for investing early on, making his first stock trade at the age of 14 from his one-year pocket money savings. While still in high-school, admittedly missing a class or two, he started building up a portfolio of stocks with an affinity for tech-driven companies. Only to lose it all in the dot-com bubble in 2000. Having been burnt from investing, he re-focused on his education: He pursued a Bachelor and two Master degrees from EBS and the University of Cambridge, graduating top of his class and being awarded various scholarships and prizes such as DAAD and Student of the Year.

Alexander started his professional career at Morgan Stanley's investment banking team amid the challenging times of the financial crisis. Being a stickler for loyalty, he stayed at the bank for nearly a decade in different roles and locations, deal captaining executions of a variety of banking products within M&A and capital markets such as IPOs, equity, debt and derivatives.

Afterwards and with his experience from MS, he supported Delivery Hero in its successful IPO in 2017 and jointly helped turn it into a DAX company, leading its M&A and VC efforts as Head and Group VP, and also being responsible for all of its corporate finance activities. This included >20 investments in growth companies with a total AuM of nearly EUR 1 billion, including successfully picking several unicorns and decacorns, among others, Glovo, Rappi, Zomato, Impossible Food, EatJust, Ola and Instashop as well as other cross-vertical investments in the FinTech, B2B SaaS, FoodTech and ESG space.

Through his bi-cultural background from living in Berlin and Bogotá, both two very divergent cultures, he feels incredibly lucky having learnt to appreciate the diversity of people's behaviour and perspective – not always picking up the best virtues of each culture, he admits.

He always had a passion for products with the ability to fundamentally change consumer behaviour such as last-mile logistics, scalable marketplaces, alternative protein or ESG in general. Given his role in co-leading the Growth Team at HV, however, he predominantly looks for sector-agnostic criteria in passionate and ambitious founders.
In
his spare time, Alexander enjoys traveling, street art and Italian wine. But mostly he likes sports, anything competitive, preferably with any type of racket.

content.text: In German, there is a special word that resonates with a global community. That word is "Bürgerbewegung" and it translates to “a citizen's movement”. For Enpal, this means a people's movement to take charge of a greener energy supply. Enpal focuses on making a literal change in the world, a portmanteau of “energy” and “pal”. Enpal is not just another solar company: It offers the first integrated solution for the green smart home, including photovoltaic panels, batteries, charging stations for e-vehicles, green electricity tariff, and energy management software. The best part of their business model is that customers rent the energy system in a subscription-style model,  saving the high up-front costs. A recent poll shows that 9 out of 10 Germans favor solar rooftop installations. Enpal works with
qualified
specialist companies and craft businesses
to make that a reality in the best and easiest way possible.

content.quote: Fighting the climate crisis is the greatest challenge of our generation. The Enpal team wants to enable every homeowner to join the fight and become energy-independent by giving them the opportunity to produce green energy without any up-front costs.

AS A FORMER ENTREPRENEUR, I EXPERIENCED MANY OF THE UPS AND DOWNS THAT EVERY FOUNDER GOES THROUGH.

YOU NEED AN INVESTOR WHO IS CLOSE TO THE BUSINESS – SOMEONE WHO CAN BE A REAL SOUNDING BOARD AND ADVISOR ON THE MOST IMPORTANT CHALLENGES.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

Before they became the first institutional investor during Enpal's Series B funding, HV Capital had developed a relationship with CEO and founder Mario Kohle for over a decade. The first interaction was during Mario's university days when he worked on a website portal for students. Not long after, Mario started Kauferportal, a platform that connects homeowners with home-related products and services, and successfully sold the company to General Atlantic. HV recognised early that Mario was a serial entrepreneur and wouldn't stay idle for long. Mario's next project was much bigger than himself and HV. He founded Enpal with the singular mission of decarbonising Europe, one solar-powered home at a time. HV loves this type of mission-driven founder, as they often possess the grit and determination needed to see a project to completion and beyond. Since then, HV and Mario have been fully unified in the mission to make Europe and the world green and energy-independent.

content.list_description: Enpal is on a mission to become the energy supplier for the 21 century and has already become Germany's largest photovoltaic systems installers. Vis-a-vis its customers, Enpal offers its "zero-down" PV rental solution with customers paying a monthly rate that includes cost of installations, operations and maintenance. This simplicity turns PV rental into the no-brainer that it should be, paving the way for large-scale decarbonization of electryicity grids.

content.text: For Enpal, the future is bright and sunny. In times of soaring energy prices and a threatening climate crisis, more and more people want to take their energy into their own hands and join the movement to protect the planet for our children. Enpal's business model of no upfront costs and low fixed-lease payments is therefore proving popular. Enpal's invention could be scaled globally and expand into other sectors like e-mobility and community-based energy distribution, connecting humankind into a renewable community.

content.text: Laura was born in the US, grew up in Germany and moved to Switzerland as a teenager. She studied in Hamburg, London and Paris, obtained her PhD in Finance at the University of St. Gallen and conducted research at Columbia University, New York. Her global experience ensures that Laura always brings a broad perspective to her work in VC.

After a stint in the VC world at Headline, Laura worked at J.P. Morgan on various corporate finance transactions – mostly across TMT and consumer industries, including IPOs, financings, buy- and sell-side mandates. Taking a more entrepreneurial approach, Laura co-founded WeSpace, the first work and community space designed for female professionals in the DACH region, for which she earned Forbes "30 Under 30" recognition.
At HV, Laura is part of the venture team where she seeks out promising startups across industries with a particular focus on healthcare and techbio.

In venture capital, Laura states money is not the differentiating factor, but rather the people who are behind the money. Partnering with seasoned investors is key - particularly when developing large, sustainable companies.

content.quote: VC IS THE BEST POSSIBLE JOB IN THE WORLD: THE OPPORTUNITY TO PARTNER WITH TALENTED, AMBITIOUS AND INSPIRING PERSONALITIES ON THEIR JOURNEYS.

content.text: Felix is always seeking companies with big ambition and the drive to transform the European technology landscape. On a daily basis he reflects on the role of VC. He channels this awareness and responsibility towards his personal interactions with portfolios, entrepreneurs and teams.

Felix studied business and political science in Munich, Singapore and London. His educational background spans the complexity, nuances and fragility of international relations. Felix graduated with a BSc in Business Administration from LMU Munich with distinction. He completed his International Political Economy Masters with distinction at LSE London.

Prior to joining HV, Felix was CEO and co-founder of a VC-backed digital learning platform, helping to build and manage the platform. He suffered and celebrated while bringing mobile learning to higher education in Europe. The company eventually sold to a competitor, and then later to StepStone.

Felix enjoys both challenging and supporting founders in their most crucial moments. He holds onto the heart and soul that he and his co-founders put into their company 24/7 over many years. At HV he has worked on projects such as sennder, Dialogue, heartbeat and homefully.

In his spare time, Felix enjoys climbing (especially bouldering), both indoors and outdoors. He also loves almost any other type of sports, including tennis, soccer, badminton, squash and beach volleyball.

content.list_description: Sdui offers schools a GDPR-compliant digital platform / app for the communication between teachers, parents and students. All important information about teaching, such as timetables, substitution schedules, letters to parents, announcements and homework can be easily shared via the platform and accessed via app or via the browser. With a video conferencing tool, a cloud, a digital class register, room bookings and other integrations, Sdui plans to become the central platform to digitalize and simplify schools’ organization and communication.

content.quote: I HOPE I CAN BE A PARTNER AND RESOURCE TO THE FOUNDER, ESPECIALLY WHEN THE GOING GETS TOUGH – WHICH IT ALWAYS DOES.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.quote: THERE ARE NO SHORTCUTS, AND PASSION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT INGREDIENT FOR WHATEVER YOU WANT TO ACHIEVE.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.text: Being born in flight, living in refugee houses, and seeing his parents start from scratch over and over again shaped Said from an early age. His parents set an example of what entrepreneurship means: having the guts and perseverance to challenge the status quo for a better tomorrow, against all odds.

Said holds degrees in Economics and Business Administration. He undertook his studies at Goethe University Frankfurt and Wharton Business School, experiencing the vivid east coast start-up ecosystem while at the latter. Inspired, he started his entrepreneurial career as the first intern in HV's then newly opened Berlin office.

Being exposed to so much knowledge in a concentrated period, Said put the lessons he learned into action. He joined a start-up as their CFO to help build the long-stay marketplace for business travellers. He was responsible for two financing rounds, gaining first-hand experience of fundraising and the emotional rollercoaster of founding a company.

Said found walking in the shoes of an entrepreneur a very humbling experience, with extreme ups and downs. It also helps him connect with other founders "beyond the pitch." When founders show passion and hustle, they will often win his support.

Said's fear of missing out on the next tech endeavor brought him to Venture Capital, where he can quench his thirst for tech-enabled improvements across different industries. When he is not reading and talking tech, Said is likely looking for the next fitness and longevity trend to try out, or watching live techno sets to kickstart his long-postponed DJ career.

meta.title: Fabian Gruner Principal
meta.description: Fabian Gruner is principal at HV Capital

content.quote: The thrill of venture capital lies in partnering with founders who push the boundaries of what's possible and figuring out how they can be supported to push just a little harder.

content.text: Fabian's passion for understanding complex systems and concepts stems from his upbringing, influenced by his mother, a computer scientist, and his father, an engineer. This early exposure ignited his curiosity about harnessing technology to tackle hard challenges.

Fabian studied Business Administration and Computer Science at WHU and TU Munich, consistently graduating at the top of his class. He also holds a degree in Technology Management from the CDTM in Munich and Columbia Business School in New York. His career began at BCG and J.P. Morgan, advising technology companies, followed by his first experience in venture capital at Munich-based growth fund Acton Capital.

As employee #1 and initial CMO/CRO at Foodora, Fabian spearheaded one of Europe's fastest growing venture scale-ups, growing the company from a single employee (himself) to hundreds in just months.  He built global sales and marketing teams from the ground up, demonstrating his strategic and operational expertise.

Since joining HV in early 2018, Fabian has  shifted his focus towards DeepTech and growth investments, particularly in Series B and beyond. His portfolio includes pioneering hardware DeepTech companies like Isar Aerospace, Neura Robotics, and Quantum Systems, as well as cutting-edge enterprise software firms such as Flip, Spread.ai, and OneData. Fabian’s analytical focus and strong network make him a valuable partner to ambitious founders on their quest to solve complex challenges to potentially change the world.
Now residing in Berlin, Fabian enjoys cycling around the city’s picturesque lakes, balancing his professional life with a passion for exploring the outdoors.

content.list_description: Hyperganic has built the world’s most powerful solution for the generative design of physical objects. On the Hyperganic platform, algorithms design objects that are as complex, functional, elegant and sustainable as Nature.

content.text: Europe, especially Munich, has a strong tradition of innovators advancing technological processes. Isar Aerospace's co-founders, Daniel Metzler and Josef Fleischmann, are prime examples. From a young age, they have been committed to pushing technology and society forward. Their paths first crossed at the WARR rocketry research lab at the Technical University Munich, where Daniel led a team of 40 students developing rocket engines and launching sounding rockets globally, and Josef with his team won the first-ever SpaceX Hyperloop competition.

By 2018, they had joined forces and launched Isar Aerospace. With the aim of lowering the entry barriers to space, Isar Aerospace quickly achieved significant technological and commercial milestones. The company has since then raised more than €350 million in private capital, making it the most dominant independent New Space company in the European Union.

Isar Aerospace's first product, the Spectrum launch vehicle, is set to transform the European space industry. Designed and manufactured fully in-house using advanced manufacturing methods, Spectrum is smaller, cheaper, more flexible and more efficient, making it an economically viable option for satellite operators. Its versatility allows it to carry a wide range of payloads, from small CubeSats to larger satellites and constellations, catering to diverse space missions.

content.quote: A competitive and diverse space ecosystem will be crucial for humanity in the decades to come. We are convinced that European cooperation, a level playing field for all players and a demand-driven approach will provide customers with access to different and internationally competitive launch capabilities for a broad spectrum of payloads.

content.text: With its more than 20 years of experience backing founders who dare to go above and beyond - in Isar Aerospace’s case quite literally, HV Capital recognized Isar Aerospace's remarkable drive and ambition during a factory tour. Their dedication to forging a new path in the space industry perfectly embodies HV's commitment to "backing those who dare." This philosophy drives HV’s investment strategy, and few pursuits are as daring as space exploration. HV takes pride in investing in innovative ventures that challenge the status quo, and Isar Aerospace's bold team, cutting-edge technology, and potential to transform the space industry make it an exhilarating opportunity that HV is proud to support.

content.list_description: Isar Aerospace develops satellite launch vehicles out of Munich with the aim of providing low-cost, reliable and flexible small satellite launch services in Europe. Utilizing advanced manufacturing methods and environmentally friendly propellants, the company is at the forefront of rocket engineering research to build the logistics backbone of the new space age.

content.text: Space represents a vast, untapped market with enormous economic potential. As the space industry grows, new opportunities emerge in satellite communications, earth observation, and even asteroid mining. Space technology has far-reaching applications primarily on Earth, from improving telecommunications to providing actionable insights into climate change. By building access to this burgeoning industry with boundless potential, Isar Aerospace is positioning itself at the forefront of humanity’s next frontier.

content.quote: I HOPE I CAN BE A PARTNER AND RESOURCE TO THE FOUNDER, ESPECIALLY WHEN THE GOING GETS TOUGH – WHICH IT ALWAYS DOES.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

The longer term goal of Dance is to spark a global movement built on a connected community of passionate e-bike riders, ultimately transforming our cities to be more bike-friendly and livable.

content.quote: CLEAR EYES, FULL HEARTS, CAN'T LOSE.

content.text: Born and raised in Cologne, David's cheerful Rhenish spirit gives him a passion and enthusiasm for new ideas. His interest in innovation led him to HV, where he channels his curiosity towards growing successful companies and teams.

David holds a bachelor's degree in Business Administration from WHU-Otto Beisheim School of Management. During his studies, he founded a promotion agency and played team handball at a professional level.

Living by the words of his former coach: "Clear eyes, full hearts, can't lose." David looks for teams who build winning companies that make a lasting impact. Every team needs clear eyes to know exactly who you are, what you do, and who you serve. With full hearts, your employees run through walls for you and run even harder through walls for your customers. Ultimately if you give it all and play like a champion you can`t lose.

David started his VC career at Acton Capital Partners, where he invested in Europe and the US. Before Acton, he did an internship at New York-based D2C brand Koio, which ultimately ended up being his first VC investment. He joined HV in March 2020.
Outside of work David enjoys long walks with his dog, Fawkes, riding his beloved old Vespa and clearing his mind in the gym.

content.text: Felix is always seeking companies with big ambition and the drive to transform the European technology landscape. On a daily basis he reflects on the role of VC. He channels this awareness and responsibility towards his personal interactions with portfolios, entrepreneurs and teams.

Felix studied business and political science in Munich, Singapore and London. His educational background spans the complexity, nuances and fragility of international relations. Felix graduated with a BSc in Business Administration from LMU Munich with distinction. He completed his International Political Economy Masters with distinction at LSE London.

Prior to joining HV, Felix was CEO and co-founder of a VC-backed digital learning platform, helping to build and manage the platform. He suffered and celebrated while bringing mobile learning to higher education in Europe. The company eventually sold to a competitor, and then later to StepStone.

Felix enjoys both challenging and supporting founders in their most crucial moments. He holds onto the heart and soul that he and his co-founders put into their company 24/7 over many years. At HV he has worked on projects such as sennder, Dialogue, heartbeat and homefully.

In his spare time, Felix enjoys climbing (especially bouldering), both indoors and outdoors. He also loves almost any other type of sports, including tennis, soccer, badminton, squash and beach volleyball.

At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.quote:
TALKING TO FOUNDERS, I REALIZE THAT WE HAVE JUST SCRATCHED THE SURFACE OF WHAT IS POSSIBLE WITH TECHNOLOGY.

HOW COULD YOU NOT BE INSPIRED KNOWING THAT YOU ARE SURROUNDED BY THE GREATEST MINDS IN THEIR RESPECTIVE FIELDS?

content.text: Being born in flight, living in refugee houses, and seeing his parents start from scratch over and over again shaped Said from an early age. His parents set an example of what entrepreneurship means: having the guts and perseverance to challenge the status quo for a better tomorrow, against all odds.

Said holds degrees in Economics and Business Administration. He undertook his studies at Goethe University Frankfurt and Wharton Business School, experiencing the vivid east coast start-up ecosystem while at the latter. Inspired, he started his entrepreneurial career as the first intern in HV's then newly opened Berlin office.

Being exposed to so much knowledge in a concentrated period, Said put the lessons he learned into action. He joined a start-up as their CFO to help build the long-stay marketplace for business travellers. He was responsible for two financing rounds, gaining first-hand experience of fundraising and the emotional rollercoaster of founding a company.

Said found walking in the shoes of an entrepreneur a very humbling experience, with extreme ups and downs. It also helps him connect with other founders "beyond the pitch." When founders show passion and hustle, they will often win his support.

Said's fear of missing out on the next tech endeavor brought him to Venture Capital, where he can quench his thirst for tech-enabled improvements across different industries. When he is not reading and talking tech, Said is likely looking for the next fitness and longevity trend to try out, or watching live techno sets to kickstart his long-postponed DJ career.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

CoachHub improves the leadership skills of managers and helps teams to work together more successfully.

TODAY THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE FOR THE INDUSTRY IS TO REBUILD OUR ECONOMY IN ALMOST EVERY DIMENSION.

THE PACE OF DIGITALIZATION MEANS THIS IS AN EVERYDAY REALITY.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

content.quote: The thrill of venture capital lies in partnering with founders who push the boundaries of what's possible and figuring out how they can be supported to push just a little harder.

content.text: Fabian's passion for understanding complex systems and concepts stems from his upbringing, influenced by his mother, a computer scientist, and his father, an engineer. This early exposure ignited his curiosity about harnessing technology to tackle hard challenges.

Fabian studied Business Administration and Computer Science at WHU and TU Munich, consistently graduating at the top of his class. He also holds a degree in Technology Management from the CDTM in Munich and Columbia Business School in New York. His career began at BCG and J.P. Morgan, advising technology companies, followed by his first experience in venture capital at Munich-based growth fund Acton Capital.

As employee #1 and initial CMO/CRO at Foodora, Fabian spearheaded one of Europe's fastest growing venture scale-ups, growing the company from a single employee (himself) to hundreds in just months.  He built global sales and marketing teams from the ground up, demonstrating his strategic and operational expertise.

Since joining HV in early 2018, Fabian has  shifted his focus towards DeepTech and growth investments, particularly in Series B and beyond. His portfolio includes pioneering hardware DeepTech companies like Isar Aerospace, Neura Robotics, and Quantum Systems, as well as cutting-edge enterprise software firms such as Flip, Spread.ai, and OneData. Fabian’s analytical focus and strong network make him a valuable partner to ambitious founders on their quest to solve complex challenges to potentially change the world.
Now residing in Berlin, Fabian enjoys cycling around the city’s picturesque lakes, balancing his professional life with a passion for exploring the outdoors.

The company is headquartered in Berlin, with an office in Belgrade. The management consists of Jessica Holzbach, Lukas Zörner, Henrik Jondell and Igor Kuschnir.
content.quote:
WHAT MAKES PENTA SPECIAL IS THAT WE AREN’T BANKERS, BUT ENTREPRENEURS. WE KNOW WHAT WE EXPECT FROM THE PERFECT BUSINESS BANKING EXPERIENCE – AND WE LISTEN TO OUR CUSTOMERS IN ORDER TO ACHIEVE THIS.

THAT’S WHY PENTA’S SERVICE GOES FAR BEYOND BANKING.
content.slogan: The digital platform for business banking.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

content.how_it_started:
Paying close attention to disruption in the SME Fintech sector HV saw a clear opportunity in continental Europe to build an SME-focused neo-bank. When HV met Penta there was an immediate click, with a shared vision of a one-stop financial shop for SMEs.

“While we have come a long way making business banking easier and more suited to the needs of SMEs in Germany, we are only 1% done. The market is still very much offline and a majority of SMEs doesn’t know there are better alternatives out there. We will work hard to improve our product together with our customers, until we are the number one choice for them as a financial partner.” – Jessica Holzbach
content.list_description: Penta is the go-to place for all of SMEs’ banking needs. Penta is more than a bank account. It’s a financial hub for businesses. Clients can run their accounting, manage corporate cards, take loans, manage their day to day business and much more through an elegant and easy to use digital product.
content.future_perspectives: Penta’s vision is to make business banking easy and digital for everyone – from larger SMEs to freelancers – so that Penta’s customers can focus less on banking, and more on their business. Their goal is to develop Penta into a financial platform where entrepreneurs can find everything they need in order to manage their finances. Services include sending invoices, cash payment solutions, bookkeeping, expense management and more.

content.quote:
GOING INTO THIS AS FIRST-TIME FOUNDERS, WE COULDN’T HAVE ASKED FOR A BETTER PARTNER. HV HAS BEEN INCREDIBLY SUPPORTIVE – CHALLENGING US TO BE BETTER WHILE WATCHING OUT FOR OUR WELL-BEING.

ABOVE ALL, HV HAS CONTINUED TO BELIEVE IN AND CHAMPION OUR VISION.
content.slogan: Your expert team's first AI colleague

content.text: Growing up in a small town in the Polish mountains, Zuzanna has always been curious to discover the world. Her determination and enthusiasm have led her to earn a Bachelor's degree in International Business at Rotterdam School of Management. She also completed a Master's Degree in Finance at Esade Business School in Barcelona. Having lived in the Netherlands, United States, Kenya, Spain, United Kingdom, and Germany and hiking to the most remote locations globally, she developed a strong appreciation for different people, cultures, and the diverse ways we experience the world. On a professional level, her desire to explore multiple paths ultimately led her to gather experiences across organizations such as NGOs, early-stage ventures, and large corporates worldwide.

She started her professional career in a start-up in Nairobi, Kenya, where she learned that the life of a founder is filled with constant ups & downs. Similarly, she developed a genuine appreciation for big ideas, the complexity of running a business, and the power of teamwork.

Before joining HV, Zuzanna spent two years in private debt and private equity at BlackRock in London. Here she focused on climate tech and renewable power investments across Europe and gained hands-on deal experience. She developed a strong commitment to working towards a better future and embraced the spirit of being a lifelong student of technology, markets, and the world. At Goldman Sachs and Global Founders Capital, she gained valuable know-how in investment banking and venture capital.
At HV Capital, Zuzanna focuses on Fintech & B2B SaaS.

Discussing disruptive ideas and meeting founders with an ambition to challenge how we live our everyday lives or run businesses across the globe are the things that excite her most. She loves supporting extraordinary visions, building long-lasting relationships, and helping others solve complex problems.
In her spare time, you will most likely find Zuzanna hiking in the mountains, reading the next best-seller, or cooking for friends & family.

content.text: Flank met HV in spring 2018 at a 15-minute Q&A organized by TU University. Back then, Flank was called Legal OS and its team of four (pre-product) spearheading a bold vision of making legal knowledge more accessible. Keeping a close eye on their progress, HV was impressed and invested a year later.
Flank has since developed a category-leading solution with strong product-market fit attracting customers such as TravelPerk, DeepL, Mural, DocPlanner, and others.

content.list_description: Flank is an AI automation platform for expert teams. With Flank, expert teams —such as legal, privacy, compliance, info-sec, and finance—can train and deploy specialized AI Agents that offer 24/7 support to commercial teams.

content.text: Every year, billions are spent on process optimization, employee training, and the latest efficiency software. However, the primary source of operational drag is often overlooked: waiting for expert support. Friction increases as the company grows. Flank’s mission is to eliminate this friction by removing the bottlenecks altogether and enabling commercial teams to make decisions (and close deals!) faster. This is achieved by empowering the business with expertise on-demand via Flank agents - a major step towards
an organization without bottlenecks

content.text: Laura was born in the US, grew up in Germany and moved to Switzerland as a teenager. After a stint in the VC world at Headline, Laura worked at J.P. Taking a more entrepreneurial approach, Laura co-founded WeSpace, the first work and community space designed for female professionals in the DACH region, for which she earned Forbes "30 Under 30" recognition.
At HV, Laura is part of the venture team where she seeks out promising startups across industries with a particular focus on healthcare and techbio.
