content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

meta.description: Fabian Gruner is principal at HV Capital

content.quote: The thrill of venture capital lies in partnering with founders who push the boundaries of what's possible and figuring out how they can be supported to push just a little harder.

content.text: Fabian's passion for understanding complex systems and concepts stems from his upbringing, influenced by his mother, a computer scientist, and his father, an engineer. This early exposure ignited his curiosity about harnessing technology to tackle hard challenges.

Fabian studied Business Administration and Computer Science at WHU and TU Munich, consistently graduating at the top of his class. He also holds a degree in Technology Management from the CDTM in Munich and Columbia Business School in New York. His career began at BCG and J.P. Morgan, advising technology companies, followed by his first experience in venture capital at Munich-based growth fund Acton Capital.

As employee #1 and initial CMO/CRO at Foodora, Fabian spearheaded one of Europe's fastest growing venture scale-ups, growing the company from a single employee (himself) to hundreds in just months.  He built global sales and marketing teams from the ground up, demonstrating his strategic and operational expertise.

Since joining HV in early 2018, Fabian has  shifted his focus towards DeepTech and growth investments, particularly in Series B and beyond. His portfolio includes pioneering hardware DeepTech companies like Isar Aerospace, Neura Robotics, and Quantum Systems, as well as cutting-edge enterprise software firms such as Flip, Spread.ai, and OneData. Fabian’s analytical focus and strong network make him a valuable partner to ambitious founders on their quest to solve complex challenges to potentially change the world.
Now residing in Berlin, Fabian enjoys cycling around the city’s picturesque lakes, balancing his professional life with a passion for exploring the outdoors.

content.list_description: WIND was founded to revolutionize shared inner-city mobility. It offers convenient, inexpensive and quick access to short distance transportation in urban areas in a variety of countries in Europe and the US. With eco-friendly vehicles, they aim to make cities a better place, by reducing traffic, carbon dioxide emission and noise.

content.quote:
AS A FORMER ENTREPRENEUR, I EXPERIENCED MANY OF THE UPS AND DOWNS THAT EVERY FOUNDER GOES THROUGH.

YOU NEED AN INVESTOR WHO IS CLOSE TO THE BUSINESS – SOMEONE WHO CAN BE A REAL SOUNDING BOARD AND ADVISOR ON THE MOST IMPORTANT CHALLENGES.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.quote:
BEING ABLE TO SEIZE THE OPPORTUNITIES WE SEE, WITH THE SMARTEST PEOPLE WE KNOW, IN SETUPS WE CAN CREATE, IS AN ABSOLUTE PRIVILEGE WE MUST HONOR EACH DAY.

WE ARE COMMITTED TO MAKING THE BEST OF THIS PRIVILEGE FOR OUR FOUNDERS, OUR INVESTORS, OUR ECOSYSTEM AND THE WORLD.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

Alasco offers a central source of information for all financial data involved in construction projects – information that building owners can access at any time to get a current overview of costs.

Peakers is able to do this thanks to the power of smartwatch data and software and is the first company training its software on actual proprietary human-to-human coaching data.

content.quote: THE BEAUTY OF TECHNOLOGICAL DISRUPTION IS THAT IT ENABLES ENTREPRENEURS TO THINK OUTSIDE OF EXISTING CONSTRAINTS AND SOLVE FOR AN OUTCOME THAT PROVIDES A GIANT LEAP FORWARD IN THE SECTOR THEY ARE IN.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

Growing up in a small town in the Polish mountains, Zuzanna has always been curious to discover the world. Her determination and enthusiasm have led her to earn a Bachelor's degree in International Business at Rotterdam School of Management. She also completed a Master's Degree in Finance at Esade Business School in Barcelona. Having lived in the Netherlands, United States, Kenya, Spain, United Kingdom, and Germany and hiking to the most remote locations globally, she developed a strong appreciation for different people, cultures, and the diverse ways we experience the world. On a professional level, her desire to explore multiple paths ultimately led her to gather experiences across organizations such as NGOs, early-stage ventures, and large corporates worldwide.

She started her professional career in a start-up in Nairobi, Kenya, where she learned that the life of a founder is filled with constant ups & downs. Similarly, she developed a genuine appreciation for big ideas, the complexity of running a business, and the power of teamwork.

Before joining HV, Zuzanna spent two years in private debt and private equity at BlackRock in London. Here she focused on climate tech and renewable power investments across Europe and gained hands-on deal experience. She developed a strong commitment to working towards a better future and embraced the spirit of being a lifelong student of technology, markets, and the world. At Goldman Sachs and Global Founders Capital, she gained valuable know-how in investment banking and venture capital.
At HV Capital, Zuzanna focuses on Fintech & B2B SaaS.

Discussing disruptive ideas and meeting founders with an ambition to challenge how we live our everyday lives or run businesses across the globe are the things that excite her most. She loves supporting extraordinary visions, building long-lasting relationships, and helping others solve complex problems.
In her spare time, you will most likely find Zuzanna hiking in the mountains, reading the next best-seller, or cooking for friends & family.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.text: Felix is always seeking companies with big ambition and the drive to transform the European technology landscape. On a daily basis he reflects on the role of VC. He channels this awareness and responsibility towards his personal interactions with portfolios, entrepreneurs and teams.

Felix studied business and political science in Munich, Singapore and London. His educational background spans the complexity, nuances and fragility of international relations. Felix graduated with a BSc in Business Administration from LMU Munich with distinction. He completed his International Political Economy Masters with distinction at LSE London.

Prior to joining HV, Felix was CEO and co-founder of a VC-backed digital learning platform, helping to build and manage the platform. He suffered and celebrated while bringing mobile learning to higher education in Europe. The company eventually sold to a competitor, and then later to StepStone.

Felix enjoys both challenging and supporting founders in their most crucial moments. He holds onto the heart and soul that he and his co-founders put into their company 24/7 over many years. At HV he has worked on projects such as sennder, Dialogue, heartbeat and homefully.

In his spare time, Felix enjoys climbing (especially bouldering), both indoors and outdoors. He also loves almost any other type of sports, including tennis, soccer, badminton, squash and beach volleyball.

content.how_it_started:
Founded in 2015 by purchasing, operations experts and German engineers, scoutbee aspired to simplify scouting suppliers. The aim then, as it is today, is to improve the transparency of the supplier network.

Scoutbee understands the complexities and the tedious, manual process in scouting and sourcing suppliers. They craved to provide more transparency and insights on suppliers, knowing that there was a better way.

They built a software as a service suite, powered by Artificial Intelligence, or AI, and Big Data to make it easy for people that need the right product to find the right supplier with the right product – in a couple of weeks…not a few months. That’s what they call it Smarter Supplier Discovery.
content.list_description: scoutbee’s innovative suite of sourcing tools supports procurement departments in meeting their most difficult challenges. From supplier searching and onboarding, to tendering and market analysis.
content.future_perspectives: Scoutbee’s mission is to apply breakthrough technology and intelligence to the procurement industry to connect the right companies from across the globe and forge better business relationships. Their vision is to improve the B2B buying process by empowering procurement leaders through Artificial Intelligence and Big Data so that they can develop tomorrow’s future, today.

content.how_it_started:
HV first met sennder in the early days of 2017 when the team started out with the idea to use empty bus cargo capacity from companies such as FlixBus to build a cost-efficient parcel network. After speaking to dozens of shippers and carriers, the team soon realized that the road freight opportunity is much bigger than that and pivoted to becoming a full road-freight forwarder in the end of 2017.

Using technology to connect large shippers with small carriers, sennder’s growth exploded within only a few months. This didn’t go unnoticed and HV joined the team’s extraordinary journey by leading the Series A in April 2018 together with our friends from Project A.

When HV first invested, the team was outgrowing a cohort of young digital road-freight forwarders set out to bring the German logistics industry into the 21st century. Over the course of the next 18 months or so, the team was able to successfully expand into new regions and build a European footprint.
content.list_description: sennder is a digital freight forwarder in the road freight industry, building Europe's largest technology-enabled truck network.
content.future_perspectives:
Utilizing data and technology, the team aims to push the logistics industry into the 21st century by building the operating system for the European road-freight market.

In 2020, sennder launched a JV with Poste Italiane in Italy and acquired both Uber Freight Europe as well as Everoad making it the undisputed #1 digital road-freight forwarder in Europe. Today, sennder manages over 40,000 trucks with offices in Germany, France, Poland, Spain and Italy ensuring transparency and efficiency within the procurement and distribution of cargo for shippers.

content.list_description: Matterway is an enterprise software vendor that liberates employees from frustrating, difficult to use software, to make companies more productive, agile and profitable. The company wants to become a leader in the nascent field of Human Process Augmentation (HPA). Its software makes humans more productive, by simplifying and automating manual tasks with Artificial Intelligence (AI) that still need human interaction.

content.text: While growing up in Rome, Italy, Jan caught the entrepreneurship bug early. After a series of misadventures, Jan set up his first "real" company at 15 with a rag-tag gang of employees from his school. The company provided IT support, sold hardware and later built custom software for clients. The "business" stayed afloat throughout university and spun out a number of projects including a video sharing site, football betting arbitrage, a bunch of websites (and a series of club nights).

Jan never really worked in a major company. Alongside his studies at HHL, he interned and worked at start-ups and VCs in Berlin starting from the late '90s – even pausing his studies for one year to help start a venture. Many of his co-interns and colleagues from that time still form a key part of his network today. Besides different startups Jan also interned at two investors, sparking an early fascination with VC.

During a PhD at WHU (which remains uncompleted), Jan started an e-commerce marketplace, Hitmeister. During his seven years as co-founder at Hitmeister Jan was primarily responsible for IT & product development. Hitmeister was later sold to the METRO group. Today Hitmeister is one of the leading German marketplaces, with over €600m in GMV.

Jan became active as an angel investor, supporting fellow entrepreneurs. A couple of years later Jan joined one of his investments, Wooga, as COO. During his seven years at Wooga the company grew from 30 to over 300 people. Jan ran various teams at Wooga, with a strong focus on Marketing and Growth, and also HR. At Wooga Jan was (among other things) responsible for a €20m+ annual, platform partnerships with Apple, Facebook and Google, building the ad monetization business, opening an office in Tokyo etc.

One of Jan's career highlights was launching a game called Jelly Splash at Wooga. In 2013, the game received over 1 million downloads in its first week, and more than 10 million in the first two months. It reached the #1 spot in the download charts in nine countries, including the US. This success made Jan fall in love with the power of software products and instant global distribution.

content.text: HV invested in Upvest in 2017, when a small team of three was sharing an office in the attic above the Factory. HV was excited to back a team of extremely solid entrepreneurs with a strong background in building products for the fintech world. But it would take almost a year for the first product to launch.

The first idea was to create a platform for ICOs – which didn’t work out, but a lot of the technology created at the time turned into what Upvest is today! At HV we strongly believe in the recalibration of the traditional, centralized banking system into a more decentralized, blockchain-based future.

content.list_description: Upvest’s blockchain APIs enable businesses to offer seamless blockchain wallets, transactions, smart contracts and data to their end users (B2B2C model). Upvest empowers anyone to access major blockchains like Bitcoin and Ethereum instantly without prior knowledge. One of the first use cases is fintechs and blockchain apps where the Upvest wallet infrastructure can be integrated as a self-custody solution with recovery features for the end-users, thereby replacing an intermediary bank.
content.future_perspectives:
The long-term goal is building a more open and inclusive ecosystem to build amazing fintech applications. Upvest’s challenge is not only building easy-to-use blockchain APIs, but rather a product which needs to fit the regulatory environment, without sacrificing on security or user experience. First, the focus will first be on making existing services as reliable and scalable as possible before extending the solution in the dimensions of tech, security, and legal.

Upvest exists to open up the financial world providing economic opportunities for all. Our goal is to make securities globally available, allowing any asset to be owned and traded digitally by anyone, anywhere.

content.about: PlusDental is a Berlin-based, leading health-tech company, specializing in the digitalization of dental treatments. The company has treated thousands of patients, together with its strong network of more than 100 local partner dentists across six countries. PlusDental is Europe’s leading brand for excellent and affordable dental treatments. It manufactures its products to the highest medical and ethical standards in its own laboratory in Germany.
content.quote: HV IS OUR TRUSTED ALLY, ALWAYS ON OUR SIDE RATHER THAN AN INVESTOR THAT WE REPORT TO.
content.slogan: Excellent, affordable dentistry.

content.quote: THE INDUSTRY HAS CHANGED SINCE I STARTED MY CAREER – FROM MANAGING A BUSINESS (TECH/BRICKS AND MORTAR), TO SCALING COMPANIES ON A LEVEL THAT IMPACTS CULTURE, INNOVATION AND PEOPLE'S LIVES.

content.text: Martin's strong personal principles and rock-solid values guided his career pathway through business and banking. He would say these elements of his personality were crucial, if not the most valuable, ingredient for his career success and his contributions towards the DNA of HV today. He has unparalleled experience within the industry, having been involved in over 100 deals.

Hailing from Southern Germany, Martin studied Business Administration in Nuremberg, graduating with honors. He followed his personal values and an interest in finance towards a career supporting entrepreneurs.

In 1994, Martin started out as Investment Manager of the VC company Bayerische KBG. The focus was on low tech: fashion companies, rail and road transportation, hotel chains, telco and next century VR companies, with clients such as Wernesgrüner Brewery, Arena and Rene Lezard. Digital transformed the industry. Fascinated by entrepreneurship and innovation, Martin moved into tech-related business. He focused on operations and became CFO of Netlife AG, the software company specializing in online banking and brokerage. At 30 years old, he was responsible for preparing, executing and managing this listed entity at c-level. He delivered the successful IPO of Netlife in 1999.

Martin has been at HV Capital since its foundation in 2000. He has played a major role in the development of the company into one of Europe's leading venture capital firms. In 2010, under Martin's leadership, the company transformed into a true partnership. During this time it became independent from the former single LP Holtzbrinck Publishing Group. He has helped some of Europe's most successful online companies on their way, including Groupon, Lazada, Linio, Delivery Hero, Spark Networks (eDarling) and Global Fashion Group. He also steers fund strategy, investor relations and capital-raising.

content.how_it_started: PlusDental has developed from a provider of cosmetic orthodontic treatments, under the brand name of Sunshine Smile, to Europe’s leading medically trusted provider of dental treatments, in collaboration with more than 100 independent dental clinics. In just over two years, the company has grown to more than 200 employees. It now operates Europe’s most advanced and largest clear aligner production in their own dental lab.
content.list_description: PlusDental is a direct-to-consumer brand providing invisible aligners that help customers to gradually move their teeth to achieve a great smile within a couple of months.
content.future_perspectives:
PlusDental’s mission is to provide access to high-quality and innovative dentistry for the general public and remove access barriers.

The founding team and HV have known each other for more than ten years. They previously built several successful companies together. When HV invested in PlusDental, clear aligner therapy was very expensive and wasn’t well known in Germany. From the outset, it was unclear how a young start-up would be able to provide medical dental treatments directly to patients. But HV bought into the founders’ belief that dentistry will, and can be, disrupted.

PlusDental believes that everyone deserves a beautiful smile. They are making the world a happier place, one smile at a time.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.about: Tourlane is Europe’s fastest-growing planning and booking service for expert-made dream vacations. It allows travelers to affordably plan and book personalized, multi-day trips online to over 50 destinations. Convenient and simple, it removes the hassle of coordinating and booking specialty travel from various operators. Tourlane raised $81 million in funding from some of the industry's most renowned venture capital firms: HV, Sequoia Capital, Spark Capital and DN Capital. They are rapidly expanding, offering multi-language service in several markets across Europe.

Julian Weselek and Julian Stiefel (“The Julians”), founded Tourlane in 2016 to shake up the industry. Seeing opportunity in the fragmented marketplace of individual travel they decided to create the ‘first global virtual travel agency’.

The Julians and Christian Saller from HV first met in 2016, after being introduced by common friends. Both sides immediately clicked: Christian had finally found the right team to back in the massive individual travel market, at which he had looked for some time. Tourlane and HV have been working successfully together since then, with Christian acting as chairman of the Tourlane board.

content.future_perspectives: With a completely new take on planning and booking vacations, Tourlane aims to become the world’s largest provider of individual travel. Leveraging technology and employee expertise customers get exceptional value for once-in-a-lifetime trips.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.list_description: Caremondo is a global digital marketplace for medical tourism that enables patients to compare treatment offers and book appointments in clinics worldwide. Caremondo partners with renowned hospitals such as the Charité Berlin and the HELIOS Hospital Group. For patients, Caremondo is a service provider, that books clinic appointments and arranges additional services such as translations, interpreter services, and hotels. For clinics, Caremondo is an international online marketing partner that generates visibility and patient inquiries from patients worldwide. In 2016, Caremondo was sold to FairMedOnline.

content.quote:
BEING ABLE TO SEIZE THE OPPORTUNITIES WE SEE, WITH THE SMARTEST PEOPLE WE KNOW, IN SETUPS WE CAN CREATE, IS AN ABSOLUTE PRIVILEGE WE MUST HONOR EACH DAY.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. content.list_description: Move24 is a moving operator targeting various European markets. Move24 operates moving jobs itself, but also falls back on certified professional partner companies in peak times. In 2018, Move24 had to file for insolvency.

Vaniday is an online booking platform that allows users to seamlessly browse for their next beauty service and book their appointment. Salons can efficiently manage their bookings, respond to customer requests and gain visibility online. Vaniday is currently operating in six countries.

content.quote: THE INDUSTRY HAS CHANGED SINCE I STARTED MY CAREER – FROM MANAGING A BUSINESS (TECH/BRICKS AND MORTAR), TO SCALING COMPANIES ON A LEVEL THAT IMPACTS CULTURE, INNOVATION AND PEOPLE'S LIVES.

content.text: Martin's strong personal principles and rock-solid values guided his career pathway through business and banking. He would say these elements of his personality were crucial, if not the most valuable, ingredient for his career success and his contributions towards the DNA of HV today. He has unparalleled experience within the industry, having been involved in over 100 deals.

Hailing from Southern Germany, Martin studied Business Administration in Nuremberg, graduating with honors. He followed his personal values and an interest in finance towards a career supporting entrepreneurs.

In 1994, Martin started out as Investment Manager of the VC company Bayerische KBG. The focus was on low tech: fashion companies, rail and road transportation, hotel chains, telco and next century VR companies, with clients such as Wernesgrüner Brewery, Arena and Rene Lezard. Digital transformed the industry. Fascinated by entrepreneurship and innovation, Martin moved into tech-related business. He focused on operations and became CFO of Netlife AG, the software company specializing in online banking and brokerage. At 30 years old, he was responsible for preparing, executing and managing this listed entity at c-level. He delivered the successful IPO of Netlife in 1999.

Martin has been at HV Capital since its foundation in 2000. He has played a major role in the development of the company into one of Europe's leading venture capital firms. In 2010, under Martin's leadership, the company transformed into a true partnership. During this time it became independent from the former single LP Holtzbrinck Publishing Group. He has helped some of Europe's most successful online companies on their way, including Groupon, Lazada, Linio, Delivery Hero, Spark Networks (eDarling) and Global Fashion Group. He also steers fund strategy, investor relations and capital-raising.

content.list_description: With Eating with the Chefs you can enjoy high-end menus, prepared by German gourmet chefs, at home. The chefs use the sous-vide method, in order to cook excellent food, ready for preparation at home. Eating with the Chefs offers a variety of courses you can combine any way you like.

content.quote: THERE ARE NO SHORTCUTS, AND PASSION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT INGREDIENT FOR WHATEVER YOU WANT TO ACHIEVE.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.how_it_started:
Moritz Kreppel, co-founder of Urban Sports Club, already knew Nawid Ali-Abbassi from HV Capital from the Berlin start-up scene. When HV Capital first met Moritz and his co-founder, Benjamin Roth, Urban Sports Club was an early-stage start-up. Their dream was to create a platform which would allow members to discover and do any type of sport at any time without borders across many European countries.

Moritz and Benjamin had created a new way of working out, exploring and finding new types of sport and studios. As a full-service provider for partners they wanted to let studios focus on what they love most: sports. They were about to prove that they would become Europe’s largest sports community. When Urban Sports Club acquired their competitor Somuchmore in 2016, David Kuczek became their partner and lead investor.

Nowadays, working out with Urban Sports Club has become the new status quo. Moritz Kreppel and Benjamin Roth founded Urban Sports Club in Berlin, Germany, in 2012. After two years of bootstrapping, the company secured early-stage financing in 2015 and went on to acquire other competitors across Europe. OneFit joined the Urban Sports Club family in August of 2019. Now, the Urban Sports Club network has more than 12,000 partners in six countries. Private and corporate customers can choose to train in studios, outdoors or online via livestream.

More than 400 employees work for the company. Urban Sports Club employs over 40 different nationalities in several locations across Europe. Moritz and Benjamin are still the CEOs of the company, actively managing day-to-day operations. They have also become business angels and mentors for other start-ups.

content.quote:
TODAY THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE FOR THE INDUSTRY IS TO REBUILD OUR ECONOMY IN ALMOST EVERY DIMENSION.

THE PACE OF DIGITALIZATION MEANS THIS IS AN EVERYDAY REALITY.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

Born and raised in rural Austria, Jakob developed an early passion for computers and understanding how they work. Experimenting with a Windows Me machine, he built his own text-based pocket monster game before he was a teenager but could never quite figure out how to add the graphics. Supporting incredibly talented entrepreneurs on their journey of developing products that transform our work and lives is what has drawn him into VC.

Growing up, Jakob spent most of his time in basketball gyms across Austria and beyond. As the dream of playing in the NBA failed to materialize, Jakob subsequently completed bachelor's and master's programs at WU Vienna and HSG, respectively, and studied abroad in Canada, the US and China.

Before joining HV, Jakob co-founded a foodtech venture during the height of the first Covid-19 wave. After selling it, he worked in Private Equity at Goldman Sachs in London, focusing on late-stage investments across Europe.
Jakob loves spending his free time in the Austrian alps, trying out new sports and is far too passionate about his AeroPress. He still hasn't lost hope that he will write half-decent code one day.

content.how_it_started: When HV Capital first met the founding team of Scalable Capital, people did not have access to smart automated investment platforms. Instead, they would have had to choose a set of ETF to strategically invest their money and rebalance such portfolios all the time. As this is almost impossible for a normal person, the team of Scalable wanted to solve that dilemma with technology. And bring algorithms so far only accessible to large customers of big investment banks to the mass market of end customers. Scalable started in the UK and Germany, became licensed by the financial authorities in both geographies and offer their service to end customers directly and through partnerships with large banks. Since Blackrock’s significant investment in the company in 2015, they partner with Scalable to sell and license Scalable’s technology to their client base. With more than €2bn Assets Under Management, the company is Europe’s leading automated investment platform. They are on the way to revolutionize the fintech market, further with the launch of their broker business in 2020.
content.list_description: Scalable Capital is a full-service online wealth manager for long term systematic wealth creation. It offers intelligent and cost-efficient investment and risk management technology that was commonly only available to large institutional investors.
content.future_perspectives: Scalable Capital’s mission is to provide a wide group of investors with access to an investment service which was previously reserved for the very wealthy. They provide a personalized, globally-diversified portfolio designed to create long-term wealth. To do this, they select the best and most cost-efficient Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs), monitor and manage customers’ portfolios continuously with their proprietary risk management technology

content.text: Martin's strong personal principles and rock-solid values guided his career pathway through business and banking. He would say these elements of his personality were crucial, if not the most valuable, ingredient for his career success and his contributions towards the DNA of HV today. He has unparalleled experience within the industry, having been involved in over 100 deals.

Hailing from Southern Germany, Martin studied Business Administration in Nuremberg, graduating with honors. He followed his personal values and an interest in finance towards a career supporting entrepreneurs.

In 1994, Martin started out as Investment Manager of the VC company Bayerische KBG. The focus was on low tech: fashion companies, rail and road transportation, hotel chains, telco and next century VR companies, with clients such as Wernesgrüner Brewery, Arena and Rene Lezard. Digital transformed the industry. Fascinated by entrepreneurship and innovation, Martin moved into tech-related business. He focused on operations and became CFO of Netlife AG, the software company specializing in online banking and brokerage. At 30 years old, he was responsible for preparing, executing and managing this listed entity at c-level. He delivered the successful IPO of Netlife in 1999.

Martin has been at HV Capital since its foundation in 2000. He has played a major role in the development of the company into one of Europe's leading venture capital firms. In 2010, under Martin's leadership, the company transformed into a true partnership. During this time it became independent from the former single LP Holtzbrinck Publishing Group. He has helped some of Europe's most successful online companies on their way, including Groupon, Lazada, Linio, Delivery Hero, Spark Networks (eDarling) and Global Fashion Group. He also steers fund strategy, investor relations and capital-raising.

Rocket Internet incubates and invests in technology companies with proven business models. They provide deep operational support to entrepreneurs and help them build market-leading companies.

Since October 2014, Rocket Internet is listed on the non-regulated market (Entry Standard) of the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. Prior to Rocket's IPO, Holtzbrinck Ventures decided to sell its entire shareholding in selected companies to Rocket and thus became a direct shareholder.

ZenMate is a free platform and device agnostic internet security solution that acts in a similar way to a VPN connection. ZenMate encrypts your browser traffic, hides your real location, unblocks geo-restrictions, provides Wifi and hacker security and protects user privacy. It is now available for Google Chrome, Firefox, Opera, iOS and Android, with other products planned for the future. It is trusted by millions of users worldwide, and won the Europas Award for Best Security/Privacy Startup of 2014. In 2018, Zenmate was acquired by Kape Technologies.

content.quote: THE BEAUTY OF TECHNOLOGICAL DISRUPTION IS THAT IT ENABLES ENTREPRENEURS TO THINK OUTSIDE OF EXISTING CONSTRAINTS AND SOLVE FOR AN OUTCOME THAT PROVIDES A GIANT LEAP FORWARD IN THE SECTOR THEY ARE IN.

content.text: Barbod’s passion for tech was already clear in his early teenage years when he started teaching himself programming and web design. A passion that has since guided him from London trading floors to the world of Venture Capital. At HV, he combines his unique finance expertise with a deep knowledge of new technologies to lead investments in the fintech space.

Born into a multi-cultural family and having lived in countries as varied as Italy, Germany, the UK and the United States, Barbod has always considered himself as a citizen of the world. His upbringing equipped him with a unique adaptability, perspective and appreciation for different cultures as well as an insatiable curiosity - especially for new technologies. Following a Master’s Degree in Software Engineering at Imperial College London he went on to receive an MBA from Columbia Business School, where he discovered his passion for venture capital.

Prior to joining HV Capital, Barbod covered investment roles in the public markets and in Private Equity. He was part of a team that backed the first privately funded submarine cable on the East African coast (Seacom) and experienced how technological innovation and out of the box thinking could do immense good, while also being a sound business. After obtaining his MBA, he took the position of VP Investment Management at Rocket Internet. In this role he was instrumental in expanding Rocket’s portfolio of companies.

At HV Capital, Barbod is a partner covering the Fintech, Insurtech, B2B SaaS sectors. He has led HV Capital’s early investments in BUX, Penta, Yapily and Solarisbank, among others. In his spare time Barbod likes snowboarding, travelling and experiencing modern and urban art.

content.list_description: Spotcap is the new innovative online credit platform providing fast and flexible financing to small businesses. The company’s mission is to enable business owners to invest and grow without having to worry about how to finance their projects. Applying for Spotcap’s credit lines takes as little as five minutes. Spotcap developed a unique algorithm which assesses the real-life financial performance of customers rather than solely looking at customers’ financial history. At Spotcap, online business owners simply connect their online merchant accounts and receive an instant credit decision.

content.text: Sven grew up in Munich alongside parents who were both engineers. As a consequence he developed a passion for technology early on that has guided him towards his interest in VC. While studying Computer Science at TUM, Sven became deeply immersed in internet technologies, and has since developed this area to become the cornerstone of his career.

Sven started his professional life as a consultant for Hewlett-Packard and was involved in a number of early internet banking projects across Europe. In 1998 he decided to go all in on the startup sector, joining Scout24 as a lead software architect. Being part of a significant startup with the mission to reshape an entire industry paved the way to replicate important learnings and successes on a broader scale.

Joining HV in 2000, Sven's initial focus was on investing in companies in the digital advertising and Fintech space. From 2016 onwards, Sven shifted his focus away from new investments towards defining the risk management function for HV's funds. Sven is currently a board member at SumUp and Semasio.

Outside the professional realm, Sven likes to spend as much time as possible with his family. He is a passionate cook and enjoys growing fruit and vegetables in his garden. Sven is fascinated by Japanese culture and strives to amalgamate this with his Bavarian roots in his garden as well as in the kitchen.

AS A FORMER ENTREPRENEUR, I EXPERIENCED MANY OF THE UPS AND DOWNS THAT EVERY FOUNDER GOES THROUGH.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.quote:
I LIKE THE IMPACT THAT A VC CAN HAVE, IT IS SIMILAR TO A TRAINER. IF YOU GAIN THE TRUST OF THE FOUNDERS, YOU CAN REACH MIGHTY THINGS TOGETHER.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

By making use of what Locafox offers, retailers can actively go about considerably increasing the number of new walk-in customers.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.quote:
TODAY THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE FOR THE INDUSTRY IS TO REBUILD OUR ECONOMY IN ALMOST EVERY DIMENSION.

THE PACE OF DIGITALIZATION MEANS THIS IS AN EVERYDAY REALITY.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

content.text: When HV Capital first met the founders of FlixBus, long-distance bus transportation between major cities did not really exist yet. In 2009 the three FlixBus founders André, Daniel and Jochen learned that the German long-distance travel sector was going to be liberalized and saw a unique chance to build up a completely new mobility service with the once-in-a-lifetime situation of the deregulation of the German market. They had little in common with the bus industry, apart from organizing bus trips to Austrian ski resorts during their student days and using the public city buses. Nevertheless, all founders were very interested in the industry and in creating a completely new means of transport. Since 2013 FlixMobility is changing the way people travel throughout Europe and the US. Based on a proprietary technology platform, a strong focus on customer experience and brand as well as the partnering with traditional transportation partners, Flix combines strengths from two worlds to form one customer-oriented service offering. In 2018 FlixMobility launched the first green long-distance FlixTrains as well as pilot projects for all-electric buses in France. FlixMobility launched FlixBus USA to bring this new travel alternative to the United States later in the same year. Today, FlixMobility is offering mobility services in 35 countries for millions of customers.

content.list_description: FlixBus is a long-distance bus operator based in Munich and Berlin. Since its official start in April 2012, FlixBus has become a major player in the European long-distance bus market. Together with a strong partner network of medium-sized bus operators, the company offers an extensive route network throughout Germany and neighbouring countries, and a unique offer in terms of quality, comfort, sales and service.

content.text: The vision of FlixMobility is to offer smart and green mobility for everyone to experience the world. To provide services for comfortable and convenient travelling to all passengers FlixMobility is constantly improving its services and investing into technology and innovation.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.list_description: Pamono is the ultimate resource for exploring, discovering and collecting extraordinary design from around the world. The company brings you material from the world’s most exclusive galleries and makers. Pamono offers design collectibles and combines vivid, original content with integrated e-commerce, while setting a high value on excellent customer service and 100% quality assurance.

content.quote:
I LIKE THE IMPACT THAT A VC CAN HAVE, IT IS SIMILAR TO A TRAINER. IF YOU GAIN THE TRUST OF THE FOUNDERS, YOU CAN REACH MIGHTY THINGS TOGETHER.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.list_description: Kiveda re-invents the way of shopping kitchens – easy, fast and comfortable. In Germany’s first online shop for kitchens, Kiveda’s customers configure their kitchen online and order it direct from the manufacturer. Offering a first class service and high level of transparency, Kiveda ensures that its customers receive their kitchen according to their requirements fast and easy and at an optimal price-performance-ratio. Through close cooperation with leading logistics and assembly partners Kiveda provides the ideal delivery service. Customers chose whether they want the kitchen to be delivered and installed or just delivered. In December 2014, Kiveda joined forces with Küchen Quelle.

content.text: Sven grew up in Munich alongside parents who were both engineers. As a consequence he developed a passion for technology early on that has guided him towards his interest in VC. While studying Computer Science at TUM, Sven became deeply immersed in internet technologies, and has since developed this area to become the cornerstone of his career.

Sven started his professional life as a consultant for Hewlett-Packard and was involved in a number of early internet banking projects across Europe. In 1998 he decided to go all in on the startup sector, joining Scout24 as a lead software architect. Being part of a significant startup with the mission to reshape an entire industry paved the way to replicate important learnings and successes on a broader scale.

Joining HV in 2000, Sven's initial focus was on investing in companies in the digital advertising and Fintech space. From 2016 onwards, Sven shifted his focus away from new investments towards defining the risk management function for HV's funds. Sven is currently a board member at SumUp and Semasio.

Outside the professional realm, Sven likes to spend as much time as possible with his family. He is a passionate cook and enjoys growing fruit and vegetables in his garden. Sven is fascinated by Japanese culture and strives to amalgamate this with his Bavarian roots in his garden as well as in the kitchen.

content.quote:
TODAY THE BIGGEST CHALLENGE FOR THE INDUSTRY IS TO REBUILD OUR ECONOMY IN ALMOST EVERY DIMENSION.

THE PACE OF DIGITALIZATION MEANS THIS IS AN EVERYDAY REALITY.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

content.list_description: With PIPPA&JEAN, women who love fashion can become independent and successful style coaches by offering products at style parties and at their own personal PIPPA&JEAN online shop. The company handles the preparation of the online shop, design and purchasing, warehousing, invoicing and the delivery of goods ordered both offline and online. Party hosts receive non-cash gifts while the style coaches receive a percentage of the turnover from a party or online shop. In 2018, PIPPA&JEAN was acquired by the founder.

content.quote:

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.list_description: Outfittery takes care of men’s fashion shopping needs. Their stylists select outfits from a wide variety of the most popular men’s name brand fashion products matching the personal preferences of the individual male customer. The selection of clothing is sent to the customer’s home, where he can then take his time in choosing which items he would like to keep. The company is market leader in Germany and most other European markets it addresses.

content.text: Martin's strong personal principles and rock-solid values guided his career pathway through business and banking. He has unparalleled experience within the industry, having been involved in over 100 deals.

Hailing from Southern Germany, Martin studied Business Administration in Nuremberg, graduating with honors. He followed his personal values and an interest in finance towards a career supporting entrepreneurs.
