content.how_it_started: In 2012 Lars’ friend Roberto invited him to a place close to Venice where Italian companies were being incubated. Depop was called Garage back in the days and the founder Simon Beckermann was sitting in a small black cube trying to revolutionize the way people shop fashion items. After many discussions about the changing fashion landscape and its consumer behavior (and some proper Italian food) they decided to work together.
content.list_description: Depop is the mobile marketplace for anyone to buy and sell almost anything straight from their mobile. If you can photograph it, you can sell it. Users follow their favourite individuals, shops and brands to discover what they buy, sell and like, or open their own little mobile shop with the touch of a button.
content.future_perspectives: Depop today is one of the world`s largest fashion communities around the globe, with more than 15 million users in 147 countries listing more than 100.000 items a day and growing. Depop is about to become the global conduit of connection, not only in m-commerce, but culture, design, and creative communities around the world. With a global community buying, selling and connecting to make fashion more inclusive, diverse and less wasteful. This is what transforming fashion looks like. “Lars’ experience and his straightforward thinking that focuses on areas of improvement are an extremely helpful ingredient for the success of Depop. We spent a lot of time together, especially during the early years when Depop was still vulnerable…I know that I can fully trust and rely on Lars and his partners who have supported and invested into Depop across all financing rounds in the past eight years, thus becoming Depop`s largest shareholder.” – Simon Beckerman, Depop Founder

content.about: SumUp enables merchants to process payments across a multitude of channels: at the Point of Sale, Online, or via contactless payment links. Launched in 2012, the company has since expanded to 31 countries, showing impressive growth. Today, hundreds of thousands of small businesses around the world rely on SumUp to get paid. Beyond the proprietary hardware, mobile and web apps, SumUp has gone on to develop a suite of APIs and SDKs for integrating payments into other apps and services.
content.slogan: A better way to get paid.

content.how_it_started: We are in the midst of becoming a cashless society. In order to facilitate this transition, SumUp has focussed on making cashless payments as easy and seamless as possible. In 2015 when the mPOS market was relatively nascent and fragmented, the shareholders of SumUp and HV’s former portfolio company, payleven, decided to join forces and pull its individual strength behind a single company. This proved to be the starting point for impressive growth over the next few years.
content.list_description: SumUp is the leading mobile point-of-sale (mPOS) company in Europe. Our company vision is to become the first ever global card acceptance brand. Today hundreds of thousands of merchants accept card payments with SumUp in 31 countries.
content.future_perspectives: Beyond scale and capturing additional markets, there is a vast opportunity to provide additional services to small merchants. SumUp’s mission is to enable small business owners, providing them with the right tools and products to meet their objectives.

The focus was on low tech: fashion companies, rail and road transportation, hotel chains, telco and next century VR companies, with clients such as Wernesgrüner Brewery, Arena and Rene Lezard. He focused on operations and became CFO of Netlife AG, the software company specializing in online banking and brokerage. content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.how_it_started:
When HV Capital first met the founding team at HelloFresh, people were either looking for recipes in books or online. They would shop for ingredients at grocery stores, or order delivery/take-out from restaurants. HelloFresh brought them something completely new that combined all these elements. It was the team’s original vision to reduce waste and bring fresh products to customers – all of which is fulfilled by the company today.
When HV Capital met the founding team at HelloFresh they were trying to find a sweet spot for consumers between recipe books, fresh ingredients and delivery. In combination with their desire to offer customers something completely new, they also wanted to reduce waste across the board.

HelloFresh started in Germany, and quickly tested in European markets before taking the big step to launch in the US amidst heavy competition. The company eventually became the market leader in all its operating markets. Six years after HV’s initial seed investment, the company went public in 2017 and is now valued at more than €8bn in market capitalization. In Q1 of 2020 HelloFresh delivered more than 100 million meals to its customers around the world.

“At HelloFresh we want to change the way people eat forever. By radically transforming the food supply chain we are offering our customers a better, easier and more sustainable way to shop for groceries. At the same time, we give them access to wholesome, tasty meals with a great value for money. HelloFresh is now a little over eight years old. In this time, we have become one of the planet’s leading providers of fresh food at home and we won’t stop here. We are very excited for everything that is yet to come!” – HelloFresh Founders

HelloFresh is a food subscription service with weekly delivery of its boxes to end consumers. It provides its customers with all ingredients and recipes needed to prepare meals at home. With focus on premium quality and ecological foods, an expert team develops exclusive recipes that are easy to cook. HelloFresh operates its market leading service in various European countries and the US.

Prior to Rocket Internet’s successful IPO, HV contributed its stakes in HelloFresh and 6 other companies in exchange for a 2.5% stake in Rocket Internet.
content.future_perspectives:
HelloFresh aims to provide households with wholesome, home-made, hassle-free meals. Without shopping, customers receive fresh ingredients directly sourced from local producers. HelloFresh contributes significantly to reducing food waste across the entire supply chain by cutting out unnecessary middlemen and providing customers with pre-portioned ingredients.

Behind the scenes is a huge data-driven technology platform, putting them in prime position to leverage subscriber touch points. HelloFresh operates a subscription business model with high flexibility around delivery. This approach can fundamentally change the way consumers shop for, and consume food. Transforming the traditional food supply chain, HelloFresh is at the forefront of disrupting a multi trillion dollar industry that’s at the start of a huge online transition.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

In 2009 Markus Fuhrman showed up at the HV office in Munich interested in a career in Venture Capital. He had an entrepreneurial background with Mjam, a food delivery service in AT. HV recommended he gained more experience as a business builder and connected him to Team Europe and Lukasz. Markus and Lukasz met and decided to start Lieferheld, the German operation with Fabian Siegel as co-founder in 2010. Sometime later Delivery Hero and Lieferheld merged. An international star was born. Nobody had any clue what Niklas, the founder of Delivery Hero and his AAA-team would build.

HV’s story with Delivery Hero begins with Markus Fuhrman. On recommendation from HV, Markus started to look for experiences as a business builder. This led him to starting Lieferheld, which merged with Delivery Hero.

Delivery Hero is one of the biggest contradictions of HV. They were somehow an enabler of the start of Lieferheld. For fund reasons HV were not able to invest in Delivery Hero as the international partner. Instead, Delivery Hero took the opportunity of an early exit, scared to stay long term for fund reasons. Delivery Hero is now a global masterpiece of a buy and build strategy. When successfully executed, their model can enable young digital companies a fast track to global leadership.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.quote: THERE ARE NO SHORTCUTS, AND PASSION IS THE MOST IMPORTANT INGREDIENT FOR WHATEVER YOU WANT TO ACHIEVE.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.how_it_started:
In October 2008, David and Robert came back from South America with their first entrepreneurial experiences and great ambitions. From an apartment on Berlin’s Torstrasse (that is still used by the company today), they started Zalando.

When HV Capital first met Zalando, buying sneakers online was anything but easy. Online penetration in the fashion industry was low, and it could take up to several weeks to get a pair of sneakers delivered. People outside of cities had to travel miles to stay up to date with the latest fashion trends, always bound to the limited offers of local retailers. Today they can have them delivered straight to their door at any time, thanks to Zalando.
content.list_description:
Zalando is the leading European online shoe and fashion e-commerce player. With its special focus on high customer satisfaction, comprehensive service and short delivery times, Zalando offers a wide spectrum of shoes, clothing and accessories for men, women and children. It is market leader in most of the 14 countries it currently operates in.

In October 2014, Zalando successfully IPOed in Frankfurt in one of the largest European internet IPOs ever.
content.future_perspectives:
Today, a world without Zalando is difficult to imagine. Since 2008, the company has grown from an e-commerce store for shoes to a platform for fashion and lifestyle with almost 14,000 employees. They aim to be the Starting Point for Fashion, and a sustainable platform with a net-positive impact for people and the planet. David and Robert are still members of the Zalando management board – together with Rubin, who joined slightly later – actively managing day to day operations. They have also become active angel investors, contributing to the emergence of several other new companies in Europe.

As an online platform for fashion and lifestyle, Zalando brings together around 32 million active customers in Europe, more than 2,500 brands and many other partners. They are aware that this gives them a unique opportunity to help shape the fashion industry for the better, and Zalando is committed to this goal.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

content.text: Sven grew up in Munich alongside parents who were both engineers. As a consequence he developed a passion for technology early on that has guided him towards his interest in VC. While studying Computer Science at TUM, Sven became deeply immersed in internet technologies, and has since developed this area to become the cornerstone of his career.

Sven started his professional life as a consultant for Hewlett-Packard and was involved in a number of early internet banking projects across Europe. In 1998 he decided to go all in on the startup sector, joining Scout24 as a lead software architect. Being part of a significant startup with the mission to reshape an entire industry paved the way to replicate important learnings and successes on a broader scale.

Joining HV in 2000, Sven's initial focus was on investing in companies in the digital advertising and Fintech space. From 2016 onwards, Sven shifted his focus away from new investments towards defining the risk management function for HV's funds. Sven is currently a board member at SumUp and Semasio.

Outside the professional realm, Sven likes to spend as much time as possible with his family. He is a passionate cook and enjoys growing fruit and vegetables in his garden. Sven is fascinated by Japanese culture and strives to amalgamate this with his Bavarian roots in his garden as well as in the kitchen.

content.list_description:

Its software as a service suite covers all relevant verticals (e.g. real estate, job listings, car) and provides integrated features to support sales and online marketing. The solutions power a number of high profile classifieds site of major regional newspaper publishers in Germany. 

In 2015, Classmarkets was acquired by ImmobilienScout24.

content.text: Rainer's habit of seeking out tough challenges led him to the world of VC. He studied engineering and economics, and worked in four different continents as a tech builder before navigating his way into venture capital. He applies a strong background in e-commerce to his work, which now spans a wide focus on anything that has the potential to become a large success or have a positive impact.

Rainer has always sought out a broad perspective across all aspects of life. Growing up with three siblings, he shared interests in sports, music and technology. His early titles included local football captain, certified ski instructor and church musician. In line with his constant curiosity, he earned a MSc in Electrical Engineering from the University of Technology, Munich, and completed his Masters at Bell Labs/Lucent Technologies in the US. He also holds an MBA from INSEAD, France/Singapore, all with the highest distinctions. His professional career started as an engineer in the mobile and fiber communications sector with Siemens. Two years later, he joined their VC from a tech perspective. After his MBA, Rainer joined 3i in their European VC team. He had also previously supported friends in an internet start-up (later sold to PageJaunes).

Rainer joined HV more than a decade ago. In his third week at the firm, HV invested in Zalando. Accompanying the founders of Zalando from seed to IPO and beyond has been the most rewarding chapter in his VC career. It taught him that anything is possible, boundaries are imaginary and amazing things can happen by working in the right set-up. Aside from this he has been involved in big exit stories with HelloFresh, Quandoo and Stylight. Some of his other highlights include working with Scalable Capital, Alasco and finn.auto.
In his spare time, Rainer is a family guy. He also likes to push boundaries in sports, participating in the Ironman World Championships Hawaii and many other endurance events.

content.list_description:

With a selection of virtually all of the leading brands, availability of many sizes and extremely high customer satisfaction, Enamora has established itself as the place to go for consumers looking for lingerie and underwear.

In January 2010, Enamora became an affiliate of 7trends.

content.quote:
AS A FORMER ENTREPRENEUR, I EXPERIENCED MANY OF THE UPS AND DOWNS THAT EVERY FOUNDER GOES THROUGH.

YOU NEED AN INVESTOR WHO IS CLOSE TO THE BUSINESS – SOMEONE WHO CAN BE A REAL SOUNDING BOARD AND ADVISOR ON THE MOST IMPORTANT CHALLENGES.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.list_description:
TrustYou is the world’s largest guest feedback platform and analyses millions of travel reviews scattered across a vast, fragmented market and transforms this content into actionable insights and data visualizations for 500,000 hotels. The products are used by suppliers – hotels, accommodations, restaurants – for an array of reputation management purposes and by intermediaries – OTAs, meta-search, destination marketers – to help travelers purchase wisely. TrustYou enables hotels and destinations to provide travelers with better services and enhanced offerings by monitoring, surveying and acting on trusted feedback of their guests, and helps intermediaries to improve travelers’ search-shop-buy experiences by providing structured data like Meta-Reviews.

In 2017, TrustYou was acquired by Recruit Holdings Co.

content.text: Lars grew up in a small village near Hamburg in northern Germany. From a young age he had an entrepreneurial spirit, striving to earn extra pocket money. This grew into a genuine passion for building businesses.

He moved to Saarbruecken near the French border to study Business Administration (Dipl-Kfm) in record time. While there he wrote his PhD thesis on the Social Construction of Trust within Organizations. Following his studies, Lars moved to Hong Kong and then Barcelona during the '90s.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.
In his free time, Lars can be found chasing new music treasures or digging in his garden. He also commits to an ongoing improvement of his karate skills.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.text: Describing his approach as generalist, but with an optic for heavy-hitting companies that can change the world, David has worked with HV on projects such as Urban Sports Club, Flixbus and Greator.

David was born in communist Poland in 1976. He moved to Freiburg in Germany when he was four. This stark cultural transition greatly impacted him. He learned to cherish entrepreneurial freedom and its infinite possibilities, while staying true to his origins. As with many former immigrants they were a permanent source of motivation in his entrepreneurial endeavours.

In the early '90s, David was influenced by his brother's obsession with computers. Instead of diving into science and information systems, David's interest was in the business side of things. He embarked on long-term studies, where he studied nightlife as intensely as economic theory. In early 2004 he worked on an MIT Sloan internal eLearning project. He taught himself programming, which he channeled towards several amateur social networking start-ups - none of them quite took off.

But his passion for the internet remained unbroken. It drove him to venture capital. He started off as an intern at HV capital in March 2005. For over a decade he shaped the German 'Gründerszene'. David participated in HV Capital's early investment in StudiVZ, Lieferheld and Westwing. Today, he led HV Capital's investment in companies as varied as Flixbus, Vaha and Urban Sports Club.
David compares entrepreneurship to a marathon. 'You have to remain patient but have a clear long-term goal' he says.

content.text: Christian's career has taken him across the opposite sides of the venture capital industry: from founding companies to investing in them. A wide range of entrepreneurial experiences has shaped Christian's knowledge of technology and new business models. His focus in VC is on travel, mobility, logistics and fast-growing companies.

Christian grew up in Munich. He holds a doctorate (summa cum laude) in mathematics and a MBA with distinction from the London Business School. His passion for technology and entrepreneurship began in 2000 during his MBA when the first internet bubble burst. Most of his classmates changed their interest to more 'promising' areas like hedge funds and real estate. Christian remained fascinated by the internet and its potential to change lives.

His career began in 1998 at an international strategy consultancy. Following stations at a venture capital company and in leading positions in two start-up companies, Christian went on to start his own entrepreneurial journey. He co-founded flight search engine swoodoo in 2007. As CEO he led the company to become Germany's market leader in just four years. In 2010 he led the sale of swoodoo to U.S. market leader KAYAK, where he took the role of Managing Director Europe. He built and managed a multinational team which was responsible for developing and growing KAYAK's product in ten countries. He was also involved in the successful IPO on the NASDAQ and the subsequent sale of the company to Priceline (now Booking Holdings) for $2 billion.

During his time at KAYAK, Christian was an active angel investor. He was amongst the early investors of GetYourGuide, one of Germany's most prominent unicorns. It therefore was a natural step for Christian to move to the investment side when he decided to leave KAYAK.
At HV, Christian is supporting companies such as Enpal, Quantum Systems, Tourlane, Roadsurfer, Holidu, Zencargo, and Flip.
In his spare time, Chrisitian loves to travel and is an enthusiastic kitesurfer.

content.text: Sven grew up in Munich alongside parents who were both engineers. As a consequence he developed a passion for technology early on that has guided him towards his interest in VC. While studying Computer Science at TUM, Sven became deeply immersed in internet technologies, and has since developed this area to become the cornerstone of his career.

Sven started his professional life as a consultant for Hewlett-Packard and was involved in a number of early internet banking projects across Europe. In 1998 he decided to go all in on the startup sector, joining Scout24 as a lead software architect. Being part of a significant startup with the mission to reshape an entire industry paved the way to replicate important learnings and successes on a broader scale.

Joining HV in 2000, Sven's initial focus was on investing in companies in the digital advertising and Fintech space. From 2016 onwards, Sven shifted his focus away from new investments towards defining the risk management function for HV's funds. Sven is currently a board member at SumUp and Semasio.

Outside the professional realm, Sven likes to spend as much time as possible with his family. He is a passionate cook and enjoys growing fruit and vegetables in his garden. Sven is fascinated by Japanese culture and strives to amalgamate this with his Bavarian roots in his garden as well as in the kitchen.

content.text: Christoph has been at HV Capital for 20 years. He has contributed to the firm in various roles and has seen the rise of the industry from the very beginning.

Growing up in the Rhineland area, Christoph comes from a family that have been entrepreneurs for more than 100 years, ingrained with a profound long-term view on everything they do. Christoph learned the family tradition early on, which had a lasting impact on him and his work.

Christoph studied Business Administration in Bayreuth, graduating with honors. He went on to work for Deutsche Bank and an international top management consultancy. Both experiences taught him the value of hard work, results-orientation and an obsessive customer-focus.

Early on, he decided to apply these values in a new field: venture capital. Christoph was amongst the founding team of HV Capital. In 2000 he was amongst the first to invest in the emerging European digital ecosystem. In the beginning, he thought the digital trend would only disrupt the media industry. He admits he was very wrong. Every year since has offered him a wealth of experience. He often refers to this ongoing learning process in his career.

Christoph has been responsible, among other things, for the fund's investments in DaWanda, MyHammer and MeinAuto, in all cases from initial seed investment to successful exit. Recently, Christoph played a leading role in the setup and financing of Ottonova, Germany's first purely digital health insurance company.

He started in the VC industry over two decades ago. At the time, he was overwhelmed by the entrepreneurial options that existed for people in their twenties. Experience only matters as long as it does not get in the way of innovation, Lars said to himself and rolled up his sleeves. In 2000 during his first years at HV as a member of the Investment Team, Lars co-founded and built up Parship which has become one of the leading matchmaking companies globally (today owned by Nucom Group).

Afterwards he co-founded Audible Germany (acquired by Amazon) and Experteer (acquired by Medien Union) before representing portfolio companies such as Care.com (NYSE: CRCM), Wooga (acquired by Playtika), Depop (acquired by Etsy), Thermondo, DELLI and Global Savings Group.

Lars knows that building a company is always an emotional rollercoaster. As one of HV's Founding Partners, he has been involved in several hundred transactions and is arguably one of the most experienced venture capitalists in Europe.

content.quote: THE INDUSTRY HAS CHANGED SINCE I STARTED MY CAREER – FROM MANAGING A BUSINESS (TECH/BRICKS AND MORTAR), TO SCALING COMPANIES ON A LEVEL THAT IMPACTS CULTURE, INNOVATION AND PEOPLE'S LIVES.

content.text: Martin's strong personal principles and rock-solid values guided his career pathway through business and banking. He would say these elements of his personality were crucial, if not the most valuable, ingredient for his career success and his contributions towards the DNA of HV today. He has unparalleled experience within the industry, having been involved in over 100 deals.

Hailing from Southern Germany, Martin studied Business Administration in Nuremberg, graduating with honors. He followed his personal values and an interest in finance towards a career supporting entrepreneurs.

In 1994, Martin started out as Investment Manager of the VC company Bayerische KBG. The focus was on low tech: fashion companies, rail and road transportation, hotel chains, telco and next century VR companies, with clients such as Wernesgrüner Brewery, Arena and Rene Lezard. Digital transformed the industry. Fascinated by entrepreneurship and innovation, Martin moved into tech-related business. He focused on operations and became CFO of Netlife AG, the software company specializing in online banking and brokerage. At 30 years old, he was responsible for preparing, executing and managing this listed entity at c-level. He delivered the successful IPO of Netlife in 1999.

Martin has been at HV Capital since its foundation in 2000. He has played a major role in the development of the company into one of Europe's leading venture capital firms. In 2010, under Martin's leadership, the company transformed into a true partnership. During this time it became independent from the former single LP Holtzbrinck Publishing Group. He has helped some of Europe's most successful online companies on their way, including Groupon, Lazada, Linio, Delivery Hero, Spark Networks (eDarling) and Global Fashion Group. He also steers fund strategy, investor relations and capital-raising.
